item.title: SHEET — 3. THE DIFFERENCE OF FORM & STRUCTURE
item.description: PAGE 3 Operation: Establish first relational proportion Form and structure represent two different levels.A form can exist without structure.A structure requires relation.The first H-D-R operation establishes the first self-relation.The self-relation enables the first relational differentiation.Potential ↓ Sphere ↓ H-D-R ↓ Self-relation ↓ Differentiation When two spheres are related through H-D-R, the first intersection occurs.The intersection enables the first inner circle.This relation can be compared to the original circle.Here we observe the first relational proportion:This proportion is established by the relation.It is not introduced by numerical measurement.The sequential order is:Self-relation ↓ Differentiation ↓ Relational proportion ↓ Representation ↓ Measurement The numerical representation reproduces the relation.It does not establish it.Example:All numerical expressions represent the same relational proportion.Form describes a coherent geometric whole.Structure only arises when forms are related to each other.It is the relationship between the shapes that enables: differentiation geometry coordinates projection further structure The first differentiation is observed before any numerical representation is introduced.The relational proportion:is therefore the primary relation.All subsequent numerical expressions are projections of the same relation.Images 1–7 show the sequential development from:Potential ↓ Self-relation ↓ Intersection ↓ Relational proportion ↓ Numerical representation The complete sequence is reproduced and verified by K2 and associated code packages. item.title: SHEET — 2. H–D–R AND THE FIRST FORMATION
item.description: PAGE 2 Operation: Establish first relation After the potential capacity, three conditions have been established: minimal complexity generative capacity self-relation The next step is to establish the first relational operation.H-D-R is a relational operator.It does not represent: a shape an object a structure It describes the first operation by which potential can relate to itself.Potential ↓ H-D-R ↓ Relation The first H-D-R operation does not produce: a point a line an axis It produces a relation between two overlapping potentials.Sphere ↓ H-D-R ↓ Two spheres ↓ Intersection Here the first relational differentiation is observed.When the relation is reproduced, the first stable structural formation is established:Vesica PiscisHere the following relations become observable: two intersection points an internal reference a stable axis a relational center The first linear reference therefore arises through the relation and not through a separate geometric assumption.From Vesica Piscis are made possible: lines nodes axes directions geometry projection The same relation simultaneously enables the structural potential which is later expressed numerically as:The relational structure is established before the numerical representation.Potential ↓ H-D-R ↓ Relation ↓ Intersection ↓ Vesica Piscis ↓ First Line ↓ Relational Structure H-D-R does not produce finished geometry.The operator establishes a relation.Relation enables intersection.Intersection enables Vesica Piscis.From Vesica Piscis the first observable structural reference is established.All subsequent geometry is derived from this relational sequence. item.description: PAGE 1 Operation: Establish potential capacity The analysis is based on the functional conditions that must be met before observable structure can exist.The starting point is therefore not geometry as form, but geometry as function.The sphere is identified as the first candidate that simultaneously meets these conditions.The sphere represents the lowest complexity that can simultaneously maintain a coherent form and preserve potential.Potential ↓ Form ↓ Minimal complexity The sphere does not constitute an end result.It constitutes the first capacity for further relational development.Form ↓ Capacity Structure only arises when potential can relate to itself.Self-relation enables: differentiation comparison projection structure Potential ↓ Self-relation ↓ Structure Potential ↓ Minimal complexity ↓ Self-relation ↓ Generative capacity ↓ Projection ↓ Observable structure The sphere does not introduce any observable structure.It establishes the functional conditions that make observable structure possible.It simultaneously represents: minimal complexity generative capacity self-relation relational potential All subsequent structures are derived from this sequence. item.description: S1 ├── README.md ├── META. │ THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN FORM & STRUCTURE │ ├── SHEET 1 │ POTENTIAL CAPACITY │ ├── SHEET 2 │ ├── SHEET 3 │ ├── SHEET 4 │ ├── SHEET 5 │ └── SHEET 6 S1 — Relational Derivation constitutes the first methodological sequence of the RP9 framework.Its purpose is to establish the minimum relational conditions required before observable structure, geometry, numerical representation, or computational verification can exist.Rather than introducing completed structures or finished models, S1 establishes the successive relational conditions from which every subsequent stage of the RP9 framework is derived.It therefore serves as the foundational derivation upon which the remainder of the repository depends.S1 establishes the relational framework through sequential derivation.Throughout this sequence, each sheet introduces one necessary relational condition while preserving complete continuity with the preceding stage.The sequence progressively establishes: potential capacity, the first relational operation, the first relational proportion, relational equilibrium, the distinction between relation and representation, and the first operational geometry enabled by the established framework. Together these stages constitute the primary relational derivation of RP9.Within the RP9 presentation architecture, S1 represents the first operational stage of the Primary Calibration.The complete methodological sequence is:S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 ↓ K1 ↓ K2 ↓ K3 S1 establishes the relational foundation.The following sequences extend, reproduce, and observe the framework established here.No later sequence replaces the relational principles introduced in S1.S1 consists of six sequential presentation sheets.SHEET 1 — POTENTIAL CAPACITY SHEET 2 — H–D–R AND THE FIRST FORMATION SHEET 3 — THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN FORM AND STRUCTURE SHEET 4 — BALANCE SHEET 5 — FIRST STRUCTURAL SEQUENCE SHEET 6 — OPERATIONAL GEOMETRY Each sheet performs one clearly defined methodological function.Together they establish the complete primary relational derivation.The sequence follows one continuous relational progression.Potential Capacity ↓ H–D–R ↓ First Relational Proportion ↓ Relational Equilibrium ↓ Relation and Representation ↓ Operational Geometry Each stage depends upon relationships established previously.No stage introduces an independent model.The relational framework develops through continuous derivation.S1 establishes the relational framework through conceptual and methodological presentation.The corresponding computational reproduction is performed by K1.S1 ↓ Establishes the relational framework ↓ K1 ↓ Reproduces the same framework computationally Presentation and computational implementation therefore perform complementary methodological functions.S1 establishes the framework.K1 demonstrates its computational reproducibility.S1 should be read sequentially from SHEET 1 through SHEET 6.Each sheet establishes the conditions required for the next stage of the derivation.After completing S1, the recommended reading sequence continues with S2, where the established relational operator is reproduced through successive structural development.S1 constitutes the primary relational derivation of the RP9 framework.It establishes the invariant relational conditions from which subsequent structural development becomes possible.No complete geometry, computational implementation, or operational verification is introduced within this sequence.Its purpose is solely to establish the relational foundation upon which the remainder of the RP9 framework is subsequently reproduced, observed, verified, and formally declared. item.title: D. H–D–R — PRIMARY OPERATOR PRINCIPLE
item.description:
This document establishes the primary operational principle upon which the relational methodology of RP9 is constructed.Rather than introducing a mathematical procedure, it defines the fundamental relational operation through which explicit differentiation first becomes possible.The document begins with Bisection as the primary relational operation and demonstrates how the operational expressions Halving, Doubling, Rotation, and Relation emerge as different manifestations of the same underlying principle.From these primary operations, the first proportional relations become observable.Accordingly, proportion is not introduced through numerical representation or mathematical measurement.It emerges as the operational consequence of relational differentiation.The document further establishes the methodological sequence through which operation precedes relation, relation precedes proportion, and proportion precedes structure.Recursive structural development is shown to preserve the same invariant operational principle throughout every subsequent level of organization.The purpose of this document is therefore not to develop the complete H–D–R framework.Its purpose is to establish the primary operator upon which the remainder of the RP9 methodology is built.The complete operational expansion—including transformation domains, scale invariance, implementation models, node-field formalisation, structural mapping, and extended operator behaviour—is presented separately within the H–D–R appendix documentation.Within RP9, the primary relational operation is defined as:BisectionWithin the RP9 framework, Bisection does not denote a numerical procedure.It denotes the primary relational operation through which an initially undifferentiated whole becomes explicitly divisible into two relationally distinguishable parts.Accordingly, Bisection precedes measurement, numerical representation, and geometric projection.It establishes the first operational possibility for relational differentiation.From this primary operation, the first operational expressions become available: Halving; Doubling; Rotation; Relation. These do not constitute independent operators.They represent different operational manifestations of the same underlying relational principle.H–D–R is not introduced as a mathematical procedure. It is introduced as a relational operator.Halving, doubling, rotation and relation do not require coordinates, numerical values or measurement in order to be defined operationally. These exist as "primary" functionsThey can thus also serve as primary operational functions"" where they operate on" or are established on top of" a primary whole" or into separated "parts" Accordingly, the H–D–R operator precedes mathematical projection. Mathematics subsequently describes the observable consequences of repeated H–D–R operations, but it does not define the operator itself.The primary operational functions established through Bisection do not create proportion.They reveal the proportional possibilities already contained within an initially undifferentiated whole.Accordingly, proportional organization is not introduced by numerical representation or mathematical measurement.It emerges as the direct operational consequence of the primary relational functions.The earliest relational configurations therefore appear as invariant proportional relations.These proportional relations remain independent of the numerical symbols, units, coordinate systems, or naming conventions subsequently used to represent them.Mathematics may describe these proportions.It does not establish them.Within RP9, proportion is therefore understood as an operational consequence of relational differentiation rather than as a numerical construction.The primary operational expressions of Bisection—including Halving, Doubling, Rotation, and Relation—therefore establish the proportional framework upon which subsequent relational structure becomes observable.Potential contains no explicit relational distinction.Accordingly, no observable structure, position, or measurable organization has yet been established.The first application of the primary relational functions introduces the initial relational differentiation.This differentiation does not create an external object.It establishes the first explicit distinction within an otherwise undifferentiated relational whole.The emergence of distinguishable relational parts therefore represents the first observable consequence of the primary operator.Accordingly, relational differentiation precedes structural organization.Structure is not introduced by assumption.It becomes possible only after the first relational distinction has been established.Structure cannot precede the operations through which relational differentiation becomes possible.Without operational differentiation, no stable relational positions exist from which structure may subsequently emerge.The primary operational functions therefore establish the conditions required for structural organization.Only after these operations have been performed can stable proportional relations become observable.Accordingly, structure is understood within RP9 as the consequence of relational operation rather than its prerequisite.Operation establishes relation.Relation establishes proportion.Proportion establishes structure.This sequence remains methodologically consistent throughout the complete RP9 framework.The first formation represents the earliest observable relational configuration produced through the primary operational functions.It does not represent a completed structure.Nor does it represent a completed geometrical system.Rather, it establishes the first stable relational organization from which subsequent structural development becomes possible.The significance of the first formation therefore lies not in geometric complexity but in operational completeness.Once relational differentiation has been established, recursive organization may proceed while preserving the same underlying operational principle.Accordingly, every subsequent structural expansion remains dependent upon the same primary relational functions introduced at the beginning of this document.The primary operational functions remain unchanged throughout every subsequent stage of relational development.Recursion does not introduce new primary operators.It repeatedly applies the same operational functions to progressively established relational configurations.As relational organization expands, structural complexity increases.The underlying operational principle, however, remains invariant.Accordingly, recursive development within RP9 represents the repeated application of identical relational functions rather than the introduction of additional operational mechanisms.Operational continuity therefore remains preserved regardless of structural scale or representational complexity.The principles established throughout this document define the operational foundation upon which the remaining RP9 framework is constructed.Subsequent documents introduce increasingly complex relational structures, proportional organization, and computational representations.None of these introduce new primary operational principles.They extend the observable consequences of the primary relational functions established through Bisection.Accordingly, the H–D–R operator serves as the methodological bridge between Potential and observable relational structure.Its role is therefore foundational rather than representational.Every subsequent derivation within RP9 presupposes the operational principles established herein.The present document establishes only the primary operational foundation required for the S1 presentation.Readers seeking the complete operational treatment of the H–D–R framework—including scale invariance, transformation domains, implementation models, node-field formalisation, structural mapping, and extended operator behaviour—are referred to: B. CODE & VALIDATION constitutes the structural invariance test suite of the RP9 framework.Following the computational reproduction performed in K2 and the systematic verification established in K4, the purpose of K5 is to determine whether the relational framework remains invariant when subjected to independent computational transformations.Rather than reproducing or verifying a single implementation, K5 investigates whether the same relational structure persists under multiple independent conditions.Its purpose is to examine the robustness of the relational model.K5 evaluates the structural stability of the RP9 framework through a sequence of independent computational tests.These tests investigate whether the relational architecture remains unchanged when different computational assumptions are varied.The package examines whether the framework is invariant with respect to: origin, representation, scaling, numerical base, perturbation, reversal, quotient relations, and machine representation. Each verification addresses one specific property while preserving continuity with the complete relational model.Within the RP9 repository, K5 represents the structural robustness layer of Secondary Verification.Its methodological position is:0. RP9. INTRODUCTION ↓ A. RP9. PRIMARY CALIBRATION ↓ K2. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K4. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K5. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K6. CODE & VALIDATION Primary Calibration establishes the relational framework.K2 reproduces it.K4 verifies its operational consistency.K5 tests whether that verified structure remains invariant under independent computational transformations.K5 consists of eight complementary verification modules.Each module investigates one independent property of the same relational framework.The complete sequence is:Origin Reconstruction ↓ Binary Pulse Invariance ↓ Start Independence ↓ Base Independence ↓ Perturbation ↓ Reverse Reconstruction ↓ Quotient Lock ↓ Machine Representation Each verification isolates one variable while leaving the remaining relational structure unchanged.Each module answers one specific methodological question.Verifies:Can the same relational structure be reconstructed from different origins? The reconstruction process determines whether varying the initial reference affects the resulting relational framework.Verifies:Does the relational pulse remain invariant during repeated binary scaling? This module examines whether the observed relational sequence remains stable throughout successive iterations.Verifies:Does the initial representation influence the resulting structure? Equivalent relational representations are compared to determine whether the framework depends upon its chosen starting form.Verifies:Does the numerical base influence the relational structure? Multiple computational bases are evaluated to determine whether the relational model remains unchanged.Verifies:How stable is the relational framework under small deviations? Controlled perturbations are introduced to determine whether the observed structure remains stable or whether the relational organisation breaks.Verifies:Can the observed structure be reconstructed in reverse? The reverse reconstruction evaluates whether the relational sequence remains recoverable from its generated observations.Verifies:Does the quotient relation remain invariant? Scaling relations are examined to determine whether proportional identity is preserved throughout the complete sequence.Verifies:Does computational representation preserve the relational structure? This module investigates IEEE-754 floating-point behaviour and evaluates whether representational residuals remain fully traceable without altering the underlying relational framework.Each verification module produces a complete documentation package containing: source code, structured datasets, execution logs, verification reports, technical presentations, reproducible audit material. Every computational result can therefore be independently reproduced, reviewed, and audited.Primary Calibration establishes the relational framework.K2 reproduces the framework computationally.K4 verifies its operational correctness.K5 extends this process by testing whether the verified framework remains invariant when exposed to multiple independent computational transformations.Accordingly, K5 does not introduce additional relational structures.It evaluates the stability of structures already established and verified.The verified invariance established within K5 provides the operational foundation required for the secondary differentiation developed within K6.The results produced here therefore demonstrate that subsequent differentiation occurs upon a computational framework whose relational properties have already been reproduced, verified, and tested for invariance.K5. CODE & VALIDATION constitutes the structural invariance test suite of the RP9 framework.Through eight complementary verification modules, the package evaluates whether the relational architecture remains unchanged under variations in origin, representation, numerical base, perturbation, reconstruction, proportional scaling, and machine representation.Rather than introducing new theoretical components, K5 demonstrates the computational robustness of the relational framework by systematically confirming that previously established structures remain invariant across independent operational conditions.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.

CODE & VALIDATION constitutes the primary verification architecture of the RP9 framework.Where K2 demonstrates that the relational framework can be reproduced computationally, K4 verifies that every stage of that computational reproduction remains internally consistent, structurally derived, and fully traceable.Its purpose is not to generate new structures.Its purpose is to verify that previously generated structures preserve their relational integrity throughout the complete computational chain.K4 performs the first complete operational verification of the RP9 framework.Its primary functions are to: verify genealogical continuity, verify proportional invariance, verify structural derivation, verify representational residuals, verify system-wide integrity, perform complete end-to-end validation. Rather than expanding the framework, K4 evaluates whether every computational result remains consistent with the relational structure established during Primary Calibration and reproduced within K2.Within the RP9 repository, K4 represents the first comprehensive verification layer of Secondary Verification.Its methodological position is:0. RP9. INTRODUCTION ↓ A. RP9. PRIMARY CALIBRATION ↓ K2. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K4. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K5. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K6. CODE & VALIDATION Primary Calibration establishes the relational framework.K2 reproduces the framework computationally.K4 verifies that the reproduced framework remains structurally coherent.K4 is organised as a sequential verification pipeline.Each validation layer examines one specific property of the same relational model while preserving continuity with all previous layers.The complete verification sequence is:Genealogy ↓ Proportion ↓ Structure ↓ Residual ↓ Integrity ↓ Master Validation Each stage verifies a different aspect of the same underlying relational architecture.No validator introduces new relational information.Every validator evaluates an already established structure.Each validator answers one fundamental methodological question.Verifies:Where does the structure originate? The genealogical validator confirms that every subsequent layer remains derived from the original relational origin and that no later construction acquires independent origin status.Verifies:Is the relational proportion preserved? This phase confirms that proportional identity remains invariant throughout every subsequent computational representation.Verifies:How does the structure develop? The structural validator examines the sequential development of the relational architecture through successive geometric and operational constructions.Verifies:What remains after computational representation? This layer isolates representational residuals produced through numerical computation while confirming that these residuals never modify the underlying relational structure.Verifies:Does the complete framework remain internally consistent? This validator confirms that all previously verified layers remain mutually compatible and structurally coherent.Verifies:Can the entire verification system be audited? The Master Validation Pipeline combines every previous verification stage into one complete audit process and provides the final operational status of the framework.Every validator generates a complete and reproducible documentation package.Each validation produces: structured datasets, execution traces, audit reports, verification files, control logs, human-readable presentations. Together these outputs provide complete traceability for every verification performed within K4.Primary Calibration establishes the relational structure.K2 reproduces that structure computationally.K4 verifies that every computational reproduction remains consistent with its relational origin.Accordingly, K4 introduces no additional theoretical claims.It verifies that previously established claims remain operationally valid throughout the complete computational chain.K4 establishes the verified computational foundation required for the remaining stages of Secondary Verification.Its verified outputs provide the operational basis for: K5 relational continuity, K6 secondary differentiation, subsequent summaries, and the reference documentation contained throughout the RP9 repository. Later verification stages therefore depend upon results already validated within K4.K4. CODE & VALIDATION constitutes the primary verification architecture of the RP9 framework.Rather than generating new computational structures, it systematically verifies the genealogical, proportional, structural, representational, and operational integrity of the framework established during Primary Calibration and reproduced within K2.Through a sequential validation pipeline, comprehensive audit documentation, and complete operational traceability, K4 demonstrates that every stage of the computational framework remains derived, internally coherent, reproducible, verifiable, and fully auditable.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.

The S4 module is organized into two complementary document collections.Although both collections describe the same Rx8 reconstruction, they serve different purposes within the repository and should be understood as consecutive stages rather than alternative versions of the same material.The recommended reading order therefore follows the progression from geometrical foundation to formal relational declaration.1. R8. FOUNDATION & ARCHITECTURE DOCUMENTS ↓ 2. R8. STRUCTURE & DECLARATION DOCUMENTS The first collection establishes the geometrical and architectural basis of the reconstruction.The second collection assumes that foundation and develops it into the complete relational declaration.Together they form one continuous presentation of the Rx8 framework.This collection introduces the geometrical origin of the Rx8 reconstruction.Its primary purpose is to explain why the reconstruction begins from the invariant reference R, how the first linear encapsulation emerges from the circle–square construction, and how this establishes the architectural foundation for the subsequent verification framework.The emphasis throughout these documents is therefore placed on: Geometrical origin Circle–square construction First linear encapsulation Operational function Repository architecture Relationship to K4, K5, and K6 This collection answers the question: How is the Rx8 reconstruction established geometrically? Once the architectural foundation has been established, this collection develops the complete structural declaration of the Rx8 reconstruction.Rather than focusing on the geometrical construction itself, it presents the sequential relational development that follows from the original reference.The documents progressively introduce: The original reference Primary differentiation First encapsulation Relational differentiation Fractal representation Numerical translation Recursive propagation Machine boundary Relational residual Final declaration This collection answers the question: How does the established geometry develop into the complete RP9 relational reconstruction? The two document collections should be read as complementary layers of the same framework.R8. FOUNDATION & ARCHITECTURE DOCUMENTS establishes the geometrical basis upon which the reconstruction is built.R8. STRUCTURE & DECLARATION DOCUMENTS continues directly from that basis and presents the complete structural sequence derived from the same invariant origin.Neither collection replaces the other.The first establishes the foundation.The second formalizes the structure.Together they provide a complete introduction to the Rx8 reconstruction, progressing from geometrical origin to formal relational declaration while preserving a single continuous methodological sequence throughout the repository. item.title: SHEET — 3. META-EQUILIBRIUM
item.description:
The observational framework has now been established.The completed relational structure has been examined through different observation classes while preserving the same invariant relational organization.The remaining methodological question is therefore:Which observation position preserves both relational differentiation and structural invariance simultaneously?The purpose of this sheet is to identify that observation position.No new relational framework is introduced.The completed framework is examined from its invariant observational reference.Throughout the observational sequence, different observation positions reveal different aspects of the same relational framework.The relational structure itself remains unchanged.Only the observational perspective varies.The objective is therefore not to identify a different structure, but to determine the observation position that preserves the invariant relational organization most completely.Within the completed observational framework, B5 and B6 represent complementary observation positions.B5 ↓ Center ↓ B6 They do not describe different structures.They describe different observations of the same invariant relational framework.The relational organization remains unchanged.Only the observational perspective differs.META-EQUILIBRIUM is established when relational differentiation and structural invariance coexist simultaneously.Δ ≠ 0 + Z = 0 ↓ META-EQUILIBRIUM Differentiation is preserved.The relational center is preserved.The invariant structure is preserved.Together these conditions establish the primary observational reference of the RP9 framework.Neither differentiation nor invariance alone is sufficient.Relational balance exists only when both conditions are maintained simultaneously.The completed observational framework therefore requires:Differentiation + Invariance ↓ Relational Balance META-EQUILIBRIUM represents the first observational state in which both conditions coexist without contradiction.The observational framework consistently distinguishes between relational structure and observable representation.Form ↓ Variable Structure ↓ Invariant Perspective may vary.Representation may vary.The underlying relational framework remains unchanged.Observation therefore reveals different representations of one invariant relational structure.The complete observational methodology now reaches its conclusion.Relational Observation ↓ Observation Classes ↓ META-EQUILIBRIUM The Primary Calibration is therefore completed.The framework has been: established, reproduced, and observed. The following methodological stage begins the computational reproduction and verification of this completed framework.META-EQUILIBRIUM constitutes the primary invariant observation position of the RP9 framework.It identifies the observational state in which relational differentiation, structural invariance, and relational balance coexist simultaneously.The completed observational methodology therefore concludes with one invariant relational reference from which the subsequent computational verification is performed.META-EQUILIBRIUM introduces no new relational principles.It confirms the invariant observational state of the relational framework established throughout the Primary Calibration.The entire S1 section can be validated and verified through the corresponding K1 folder" which goes by the name" A. Together these stages complete the primary observational framework of RP9.Within the RP9 presentation architecture, S3 concludes the Primary Calibration.The complete methodological sequence is:S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 ↓ K1 ↓ K2 ↓ K3 S1 establishes the relational framework.S2 reproduces the established framework through successive relational development.S3 observes the completed framework without modifying its relational organization.The computational verification begins only after this observational sequence has been completed.This sequence consists of three complementary presentation sheets.SHEET 1 — RELATIONAL OBSERVATION SHEET 2 — OBSERVATION CLASSES SHEET 3 — META-EQUILIBRIUM Each sheet performs one clearly defined methodological function.Together they establish the complete observational methodology of the RP9 framework.Introduces the transition from relational derivation to relational observation.The completed relational framework becomes the object of observation.No new relations or structures are introduced.Introduces the observation classes through which the same relational framework may be examined.The relational structure remains invariant while the observation position changes.This establishes the observational reference system used throughout the continued presentation.Identifies the observation position that simultaneously preserves differentiation and structural invariance.The sequence concludes with the establishment of META-EQUILIBRIUM as the primary observational reference for the continued verification chain.The observational methodology follows one continuous relational sequence.Established Relational Framework ↓ Relational Observation ↓ Observation Classes ↓ Invariant Observation ↓ META-EQUILIBRIUM The relational framework itself remains unchanged throughout the sequence.Only the observational perspective develops.S3 establishes the conceptual methodology of relational observation.The corresponding computational implementation is reproduced and verified within K3.S3 ↓ Establishes the observational methodology ↓ K3 ↓ Computationally reproduces and verifies the observational framework Presentation and computational implementation therefore perform complementary methodological functions.S3 defines the observational principles.K3 reproduces and verifies those principles computationally.S3 should be read sequentially.SHEET 1 ↓ SHEET 2 ↓ SHEET 3 Each sheet extends the previous one.Together they complete the observational framework established throughout the Primary Calibration.After completing S3, the recommended reading sequence continues with K1, where the relational framework begins its computational reproduction and operational verification.S3 constitutes the observational stage of the RP9 Primary Calibration.It demonstrates how one invariant relational framework may be examined through different observation positions without altering its underlying relational organization.The sequence item.title: SHEET — 3. Structural Interpretation
item.description:
The purpose of this presentation is not only to visualize the progressive development of the H–D–R operator, but also to clarify the relational significance of the completed structural framework.The successive H–D–R operations establish a relational structure that gradually reaches its complete structural capacity.The significance of this completion is not the creation of additional geometry, but the establishment of a relational framework from which subsequent structural observations become possible.Within RP9, relations are established before projections.The intersection points generated through repeated applications of the H–D–R operator create the relational framework from which linear, planar and volumetric structures may subsequently be expressed.Projection therefore follows relation.It does not generate it.A fundamental distinction is maintained throughout the RP9 framework between structure and form.The relational structure constitutes the invariant framework.The observable form represents the variable configuration through which that invariant structure is expressed.Changes in orientation, projection or representation therefore modify the form, while the underlying relational organization remains unchanged.Structure is invariant.Form is variable.Once the fifth H–D–R operation has been completed, the relational framework possesses the capacity to express both planar and volumetric organization through the same underlying relational system.Within this framework, the dual square represents the complete two-dimensional relational reference.The dual cube represents the corresponding three-dimensional relational reference.Together they constitute the primary structural framework used throughout the continued RP9 presentation.The completed relational framework establishes the common structural reference through which both the internal Base-8 organization and the observable Base-10 projection are described within RP9.The invariant relational organization remains unchanged.Only its projected representation differs.The presentation therefore distinguishes between the relational structure itself and the coordinate systems through which that structure is observed.Once the invariant relational framework has been established, subsequent structural configurations are not introduced as independent constructions.They represent different relational projections of the same underlying structure.The structural possibilities are therefore already contained within the established relational framework.Further development increases the number of observable relations rather than introducing new structural principles.The figures presented throughout this document are intentionally limited to the smallest set of structural stages required to illustrate the completed relational framework.This reduction serves only pedagogical purposes.No relational information is removed.The complete structural derivation, sequential generation, metadata and computational verification remain fully available within the K2 code base.The present document therefore functions as a visual interpretation of an already established relational structure rather than an independent structural derivation.The entire S1 section can be validated and verified through the corresponding K1 folder" which goes by the name" A. item.description:
S2 — Relational Reproduction constitutes the second methodological sequence of the RP9 framework.Its purpose is to demonstrate how the relational framework established in S1 is progressively reproduced through repeated application of the invariant H–D–R operator.Unlike S1, which establishes the relational conditions required for structure, S2 demonstrates how those established relations successively enable increasing structural capacity without introducing new relational principles.The sequence therefore illustrates structural development through relational continuity rather than through the creation of new structures.S2 reproduces the previously established relational framework through successive structural expansion.Throughout the sequence, the H–D–R operator remains unchanged.What changes is the number of possible relational connections generated through repeated application of the same invariant operation.The sequence progressively demonstrates: successive relational reproduction, increasing structural capacity, emergence of the complete relational framework, establishment of the Core4 reference model, and the distinction between relational structure and its observable projections. Together these stages establish the complete structural reference used throughout the remainder of the RP9 framework.Within the RP9 presentation architecture, S2 extends the relational derivation established by S1.The complete methodological sequence is:S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 ↓ K1 ↓ K2 ↓ K3 S1 establishes the relational framework.S2 reproduces and expands that framework through repeated relational operations.S3 subsequently examines the completed structure through systematic observation.This folder contains four complementary documents.A. SEQUENCE 2 ↓ A. COMPRESSED VISUAL PRESENTATION ↓ C. item.title: INTRO IMAGES
item.description:
R8.A introduces the fundamental geometrical construction from which the Rx8 reconstruction originates.Beginning with a single invariant radius R, the circle is enclosed by its minimal square whose side length equals the circle's diameter, 2R. The resulting perimeter therefore becomes 8R, establishing the first complete linear encapsulation generated directly from the original radial reference.The significance of this construction does not lie in the numerical value itself.Its significance lies in the transition from continuous circular geometry to the first complete linear reference framework capable of supporting differentiation, measurement, relational reconstruction, and recursive propagation.Within the RP9 framework, R8.A serves as the geometrical foundation upon which the complete Rx8 reconstruction is developed.
R8.B provides a condensed architectural overview of the complete Rx8 reconstruction.Rather than presenting the full geometrical derivation, it summarizes the principal concepts, operational functions, structural relationships, and sequential development that define the Rx8 framework.Beginning with the original geometrical reference R, the overview follows the progression toward the first linear encapsulation Rx8, establishing the methodological foundation for relational differentiation, structural representation, recursive reconstruction, and the subsequent verification architecture developed throughout RP9.Within the repository, R8.B functions as the architectural introduction to the complete Rx8 documentation, providing the conceptual context required for the detailed declarations and verification presented in the accompanying documents. item.description: This final declaration does not introduce a new relational model.It does not introduce a new verification.It does not introduce a new mathematical representation.The purpose is to summarize the methodological position through which RP9 presents its work and to conclude the relational declaration.RP9 declares a coherent relational model.The model is treated as a sequentially derived structure where each established function can be traced back to previously defined relations.No part is treated in isolation.No part is introduced without relation to the structure through which it was established.The presentation of the project is therefore based on a coherent chain of derivation where definition, relation, structure, projection, representation and verification are treated as mutually dependent parts of the same model.The relational model thus constitutes the common reference through which all presentation, representation and verification layers of the project are organized.RP9's verification architecture is built for reproduction, verification and documentation.The project distinguishes between: A. Primary calibration, B. Secondary verification, C. Relational Appendix. This division does not aim to divide the model.It aims to organize it.Through this structure, the same relational model can be followed through presentation, code, mathematical notation, documentation and supplementary material without changing the underlying structure.Each verification layer thus fulfills a specific methodological function while all layers describe the same previously established model.RP9 declares that the project's work should be understood as a coherent relational derivation.The project declares its position through the model, the method, the presentation order and the verification architecture that have been previously established.RP9 therefore does not treat the current issue as an isolated problem disconnected from the structure through which the issue arises.From a relational perspective, an issue can only be understood through the structure that enables its formulation, representation and observation.The project's declared position is therefore that the relational model constitutes the basis through which the current issue is addressed.In this sense, the term resolution is used as a methodological description of the project's working method.Resolution does not mean that an individual relation is isolated or that an individual element alone constitutes the project's result.Instead, the term describes the process through which an issue is returned to the relational structure from which it is derived and organized.The coherent relational model thus constitutes the project's declared frame of reference.How this model is assessed, analyzed or evaluated is left to the reader.RP9 therefore concludes the declaration by referring to the complete presentation, verification and documentation structure previously established throughout all parts of the project. item.description:
The S-series constitutes the primary presentation sequence of the RP9 relational framework.Its purpose is to establish, reproduce, and observe the invariant relational framework before any computational implementation or operational verification is introduced.The sequence therefore represents the conceptual foundation of the Primary Calibration.Rather than presenting independent theories or isolated models, each sequence performs one clearly defined methodological function within one continuous relational architecture.Together they establish the complete presentation layer upon which the corresponding code bases are subsequently reproduced and verified.The S-series is organised into three complementary methodological sequences.Each sequence extends the previous one without modifying the invariant relational framework.S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 Together they establish: the relational foundation, the complete structural framework, and the observational methodology of RP9. The computational verification begins only after this presentation sequence has been completed.Each sequence performs one unique methodological responsibility.S1 establishes the minimum relational conditions required for observable structure to exist.The sequence derives the relational framework from potential capacity through the first operational geometry.It establishes the invariant relational foundation of RP9.S2 demonstrates how the established relational framework is progressively reproduced through repeated application of the invariant H–D–R operator.No new relational principles are introduced.Successive reproduction increases structural capacity while preserving the same underlying relational organisation.The completed framework establishes Core4 as the primary structural reference.S3 examines the completed relational framework through systematic observation.The relational structure remains invariant while the observational perspective changes.The sequence concludes with the establishment of META-EQUILIBRIUM as the primary observational reference for the continued verification chain.The presentation sequences and computational implementations perform complementary methodological functions.S1 ↓ K1 ↓ S2 ↓ K2 ↓ S3 ↓ K3 The presentation establishes the framework.The code bases reproduce and verify the same framework computationally.Each code base corresponds directly to the sequence that precedes it.This preserves complete methodological traceability throughout the Primary Calibration.The S-series should be read sequentially.S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 Each sequence depends upon the relational framework established previously.Only after completing the complete presentation sequence should the reader proceed to the corresponding computational verification contained within the K-series.Within the RP9 presentation architecture, the S-series occupies the first operational stage of the Primary Calibration.0. RP9. INTRODUCTION ↓ A. PRIMARY CALIBRATION ↓ S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 ↓ K1 ↓ K2 ↓ K3 The S-series therefore establishes the complete conceptual framework that is subsequently reproduced, verified, and operationally validated through the associated code bases.The S-series constitutes the primary presentation architecture of the RP9 framework.S1 establishes the invariant relational foundation.S2 reproduces the completed structural framework.S3 establishes the observational methodology through which that framework is examined.Together these three methodological sequences form one continuous relational presentation that prepares the framework for its computational reproduction and verification. The Secondary Verification repository extends the methodological foundation established within the Primary Calibration.It does not introduce an independent framework.Instead, it demonstrates how the relational foundation established by RP9 can be reconstructed, formalized and computationally verified through successive structural layers.The repository is organized into two complementary sections.B. RP9. SECONDARY VERIFICATION ├── B. A. THE SEQUENCES (S-series) │ └── B. B. CODE & VALIDATION (K-series) Both sections describe the same verification architecture from different perspectives.The first establishes the structural sequence.The second establishes the computational verification.The S-series provides the conceptual and structural presentation of the verification architecture.Rather than beginning with executable code, these documents establish the geometrical, relational and architectural sequence upon which the verification framework is constructed.The collection currently contains the S4 presentation together with two complementary document series.S4 ↓ R8. FOUNDATION & ARCHITECTURE DOCUMENTS ↓ R8. STRUCTURE & DECLARATION DOCUMENTS Together these documents explain: the geometrical origin, the architectural framework, the structural reconstruction, and the complete relational declaration. The S-series therefore explains the verification architecture before computational validation begins.The K-series contains the executable verification framework.Where the S-series explains the structural sequence conceptually, the K-series reproduces that same sequence computationally.The verification framework currently consists of:K2 ↓ K4 ↓ K5 ↓ K6 These modules provide: computational reconstruction, structural validation, invariance analysis, recursive verification, machine reproducibility, and second differentiation. Each module extends the previous stage while preserving a continuous verification chain.The two sections should not be interpreted as independent repository branches.They perform complementary functions within the same verification architecture.Primary Calibration ↓ Relational Foundation ↓ Secondary Verification ├── S-series │ Structural Presentation │ └── K-series Computational Verification The S-series establishes the structural sequence.The K-series validates that sequence computationally.Together they constitute the complete Secondary Verification architecture.The recommended reading order is:Primary Calibration ↓ S-series ↓ K-series Readers unfamiliar with the verification framework should begin with the S-series before proceeding to the computational validation modules.The Secondary Verification repository demonstrates how the relational framework established by RP9 is reconstructed through sequential documentation and verified through reproducible computational analysis.The structural presentation and the computational validation describe the same framework from complementary perspectives.One explains.The other verifies. item.description:
RP9 FRAMEWORK RELATIONAL PRESENTATION ARCHITECTURE ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ A. PRIMARY CALIBRATION Establishes the relational framework │ ▼ B. SECONDARY VERIFICATION Reproduces, extends and verifies the framework │ ▼ C. RP9. SUMMARIES Organises, connects and formally declares RP9 │ ▼ D. RELATIONAL APPENDIX Visualisations • Documentation • References • Deepening ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Four complementary layers — One relational framework Primary Calibration constitutes the primary presentation and computational calibration of the RP9 relational framework.Its purpose is to establish the invariant relational framework, reproduce it computationally, and prepare it for the complete verification performed within the Secondary Verification.Rather than presenting independent models, Primary Calibration develops one continuous relational framework through successive methodological stages.The result is the minimum complete presentation required to establish the framework before its extended computational analysis and verification.Primary Calibration is organised into two complementary methodological layers.A. THE SEQUENCES (S-series) ↓ B. CODE & VALIDATION (K-series) The S-series establishes the relational framework through conceptual and methodological presentation.The K-series reproduces the same framework computationally and provides the primary operational validation.Together these two layers constitute the complete Primary Calibration.The S-series establishes the conceptual presentation of the RP9 framework through three sequential methodological stages.S1 ↓ S2 ↓ S3 Establishes the invariant relational foundation from potential capacity through the first operational geometry.Demonstrates how the invariant H–D–R operator progressively reproduces the complete structural framework while preserving relational continuity.Within the Primary Calibration, S2 is intentionally presented as a condensed reference edition.The complete structural derivation is provided within the corresponding section of B. RP9. SECONDARY VERIFICATION.Establishes the observational methodology through which the completed relational framework is examined while preserving structural invariance.The sequence concludes with the establishment of META-EQUILIBRIUM as the primary observational reference.The K-series reproduces the framework established by the presentation sequences through computational implementation.Each code base corresponds directly to the presentation sequence that precedes it.S1 → K1 S2 → K2 S3 → K3 Computationally reproduces the relational derivation established within S1.Provides the computational structural reference generated through the invariant H–D–R sequence.Within the Primary Calibration, K2 is intentionally presented as a condensed reference edition.The complete computational derivation, metadata, validation, and supporting documentation are provided within B. RP9. SECONDARY VERIFICATION → K2. CODE & VALIDATION.Computationally reproduces the observational methodology established within S3 and performs the primary operational validation of the completed relational framework.The complete Primary Calibration follows one continuous methodological sequence.S1 ↓ K1 ↓ S2 ↓ K2 ↓ S3 ↓ K3 Presentation and computational implementation therefore remain continuously synchronised throughout the calibration process.Each computational stage reproduces the relational framework established immediately beforehand.Primary Calibration establishes the complete relational framework and its primary computational implementation.The complete structural derivations, extended computational analyses, validation chains, supporting metadata, and supplementary documentation are intentionally organised within:B. RP9. SECONDARY VERIFICATION Primary Calibration therefore presents the minimum complete framework required to establish and understand RP9, while Secondary Verification provides its complete computational reproduction and extended verification.The recommended reading sequence is:0. RP9. INTRODUCTION ↓ A. THE SEQUENCES (S-series) ↓ B. CODE & VALIDATION (K-series) ↓ B. RP9. SECONDARY VERIFICATION This sequence preserves complete methodological continuity throughout the repository.The Primary Calibration constitutes the first operational layer of the RP9 framework.Through the combined presentation of the S-series and the computational implementation of the K-series, it establishes the invariant relational framework, reproduces it computationally, and prepares it for the complete structural verification contained within the Secondary Verification.Together these complementary layers provide the complete methodological foundation upon which the remainder of the RP9 repository is constructed. item.title: 3.A. Core4X (X-Y-Z). PYTHON
item.description: # ============================================================ # 3.B. VP Core4 (X-Y-Z) SEQ META Render # META + IMAGE + HTML SEQUENTIAL RENDER SYSTEM # ============================================================ # # STEP_0 = CIRCLES # STEP_1 = INTERSECTIONS # STEP_2 = XY_GROUP_LINES # STEP_3 = XYZ_DIAGONALS # # EACH STEP EXPORTS: # # /HTML # /PNG # /META # # FEATURES: # # 1. Sequential HTML traversal # 2. Four PNG renders per step # 3. Metadata render per step # 4. CSV + JSON exports # 5. Back / Next controls # # ============================================================ import csv import json import subprocess import sys import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go import plotly.io as pio pio.renderers.default = "browser" # ============================================================ # GLOBAL SETTINGS # ============================================================ SCRIPT_VERSION = "4.0.0" try: SCRIPT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve() except NameError: SCRIPT_PATH = Path.cwd() / "VP_Core4_XYZ_SEQUENCE.py" ROOT_DIR = SCRIPT_PATH.parent ROOT_EXPORT = ROOT_DIR / "VP_Core4_XYZ_SEQUENCE" ROOT_EXPORT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) # ============================================================ # RENDER SETTINGS # ============================================================ RADIUS = 1.5 NUM_POINTS = 600 COLOR_BACKGROUND = "black" COLOR_CIRCLE = "#00ff66" COLOR_INNER = "#00aaff" COLOR_LEVEL2 = "#ffffff" COLOR_LEVEL3 = "#ff8800" COLOR_OUTER = "#ff0033" COLOR_LINES = "#ffffff" ROTATIONS = [ (45.0, 45.0, 0.0), (45.0, -45.0, 0.0), (-45.0, 45.0, 0.0), (-45.0, -45.0, 0.0) ] # ============================================================ # CAMERA VIEWS # ============================================================ CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": { "camera": dict( eye=dict( x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE ) ) }, "V-B": { "camera": dict( eye=dict( x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0 ) ) }, "V-C": { "camera": dict( eye=dict( x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0 ) ) }, "V-D": { "camera": dict( eye=dict( x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE ) ) } } # ============================================================ # KALEIDO # ============================================================ def ensure_kaleido(): try: import kaleido return True except Exception: subprocess.check_call([ sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido" ]) return True # ============================================================ # ROTATION MATRIX # ============================================================ def rotation_matrix(ax_deg, ay_deg, az_deg): ax = np.deg2rad(ax_deg) ay = np.deg2rad(ay_deg) az = np.deg2rad(az_deg) rx = np.array([ [1,0,0], [0,np.cos(ax),-np.sin(ax)], [0,np.sin(ax), np.cos(ax)] ]) ry = np.array([ [ np.cos(ay),0,np.sin(ay)], [0,1,0], [-np.sin(ay),0,np.cos(ay)] ]) rz = np.array([ [np.cos(az),-np.sin(az),0], [np.sin(az), np.cos(az),0], [0,0,1] ]) return rz @ ry @ rx # ============================================================ # BUILD CIRCLES # ============================================================ def build_circles(radius, rotations): circles = [] base_centers = [ np.array([-radius/2,0,0]), np.array([ radius/2,0,0]) ] base_ex = np.array([1,0,0]) base_ey = np.array([0,1,0]) base_n = np.array([0,0,1]) for rot in rotations: r = rotation_matrix(*rot) ex = r @ base_ex ey = r @ base_ey n = r @ base_n for c in base_centers: circles.append({ "center": r @ c, "ex": ex / np.linalg.norm(ex), "ey": ey / np.linalg.norm(ey), "normal": n / np.linalg.norm(n), "radius": radius }) return circles # ============================================================ # SAMPLE CIRCLE # ============================================================ def sample_circle(circle): t = np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,NUM_POINTS) c = circle["center"] ex = circle["ex"] ey = circle["ey"] r = circle["radius"] pts = ( c.reshape(3,1) + r*np.cos(t)*ex.reshape(3,1) + r*np.sin(t)*ey.reshape(3,1) ) return pts[0], pts[1], pts[2] # ============================================================ # INTERSECTION # ============================================================ def circle_intersection(ca, cb): c1 = ca["center"] c2 = cb["center"] n1 = ca["normal"] n2 = cb["normal"] r = ca["radius"] d = np.cross(n1,n2) dn = np.linalg.norm(d) if dn < 1e-8: return [] d = d / dn A = np.vstack([n1,n2,d]) B = np.array([ np.dot(n1,c1), np.dot(n2,c2), 0 ]) try: p0 = np.linalg.solve(A,B) except: p0 = np.linalg.lstsq(A,B,rcond=None)[0] m = p0 - c1 a = np.dot(d,d) b = 2*np.dot(m,d) c = np.dot(m,m)-r*r disc = b*b - 4*a*c if disc < 0: return [] disc = max(disc,0) s = np.sqrt(disc) t1 = (-b+s)/(2*a) t2 = (-b-s)/(2*a) pts = [ p0+t1*d, p0+t2*d ] out=[] for p in pts: if abs(np.linalg.norm(p-c2)-r) < 1e-5: if not any(np.linalg.norm(p-q)<1e-6 for q in out): out.append(p) return out # ============================================================ # COMPUTE INTERSECTIONS # ============================================================ def compute_intersections(circles): pts=[] for i in range(len(circles)): for j in range(i+1,len(circles)): pts += circle_intersection( circles[i], circles[j] ) unique=[] for p in pts: if not any(np.linalg.norm(p-q)<1e-6 for q in unique): unique.append(p) return unique # ============================================================ # CLASSIFY # ============================================================ def classify(points): d=[np.linalg.norm(p) for p in points] shells=sorted(set(np.round(d,6))) inner=[] level2=[] level3=[] outer=[] for p,r in zip(points,d): r=np.round(r,6) if abs(r-shells[0])<1e-6: inner.append(p) elif abs(r-shells[1])<1e-6: level2.append(p) elif abs(r-shells[2])<1e-6: level3.append(p) else: outer.append(p) return inner,level2,level3,outer # ============================================================ # DRAW NODES # ============================================================ def draw_nodes(traces,nodes,color,size): if len(nodes)==0: return traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in nodes], y=[p[1] for p in nodes], z=[p[2] for p in nodes], mode="markers", marker=dict( size=size, color=color ), showlegend=False )) # ============================================================ # EDGE LINKS # ============================================================ def link_nodes(traces,nodes,color,width=2,opacity=0.5): if len(nodes)<2: return pts=np.array(nodes) d=[] for i in range(len(pts)): for j in range(i+1,len(pts)): dist=np.linalg.norm(pts[i]-pts[j]) if dist>1e-6: d.append(dist) if len(d)==0: return mind=min(d) thresh=mind*1.08 for i in range(len(pts)): for j in range(i+1,len(pts)): dist=np.linalg.norm(pts[i]-pts[j]) if dist<=thresh: traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[pts[i][0],pts[j][0]], y=[pts[i][1],pts[j][1]], z=[pts[i][2],pts[j][2]], mode="lines", line=dict( color=color, width=width ), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False )) # ============================================================ # DIAGONAL LINKS # ============================================================ def link_diagonals(traces,nodes,color,width=2,opacity=0.45): if len(nodes)<3: return pts=np.array(nodes) distances=[] for i in range(len(pts)): for j in range(i+1,len(pts)): dist=np.linalg.norm(pts[i]-pts[j]) if dist>1e-6: distances.append(dist) if len(distances)==0: return edge=min(distances) for i in range(len(pts)): for j in range(i+1,len(pts)): dist=np.linalg.norm(pts[i]-pts[j]) if dist>edge*1.08: traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[pts[i][0],pts[j][0]], y=[pts[i][1],pts[j][1]], z=[pts[i][2],pts[j][2]], mode="lines", line=dict( color=color, width=width ), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False )) # ============================================================ # BUILD STRUCTURE # ============================================================ circles=build_circles(RADIUS,ROTATIONS) points=compute_intersections(circles) inner,level2,level3,outer=classify(points) # ============================================================ # STEP DEFINITIONS # ============================================================ STEP_DEFINITIONS = [ { "id": "STEP_0_CIRCLES", "layers": [ "circles" ] }, { "id": "STEP_1_INTERSECTIONS", "layers": [ "circles", "nodes" ] }, { "id": "STEP_2_XY_RELATIONS", "layers": [ "circles", "nodes", "xy" ] }, { "id": "STEP_3_XYZ_DIAGONALS", "layers": [ "circles", "nodes", "xy", "xyz" ] } ] # ============================================================ # BUILD FIGURE # ============================================================ def build_step_figure(step_layers): traces=[] # ------------------------------------------------ # CIRCLES # ------------------------------------------------ if "circles" in step_layers: for c in circles: x,y,z=sample_circle(c) traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=x, y=y, z=z, mode="lines", line=dict( color=COLOR_CIRCLE, width=4 ), opacity=0.9, showlegend=False )) # ------------------------------------------------ # NODES # ------------------------------------------------ if "nodes" in step_layers: draw_nodes(traces,inner,COLOR_INNER,6) draw_nodes(traces,level2,COLOR_LEVEL2,6) draw_nodes(traces,level3,COLOR_LEVEL3,6) draw_nodes(traces,outer,COLOR_OUTER,7) # ------------------------------------------------ # XY # ------------------------------------------------ if "xy" in step_layers: link_nodes(traces,inner,COLOR_INNER) link_nodes(traces,level2,COLOR_LEVEL2) link_nodes(traces,level3,COLOR_LEVEL3) link_nodes(traces,outer,COLOR_OUTER) # ------------------------------------------------ # XYZ # ------------------------------------------------ if "xyz" in step_layers: link_diagonals(traces,inner,COLOR_INNER) link_diagonals(traces,level2,COLOR_LEVEL2) link_diagonals(traces,level3,COLOR_LEVEL3) link_diagonals(traces,outer,COLOR_OUTER) fig=go.Figure(data=traces) fig.update_layout( paper_bgcolor=COLOR_BACKGROUND, plot_bgcolor=COLOR_BACKGROUND, width=1100, height=650, margin=dict( l=0, r=0, t=40, b=0 ), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor=COLOR_BACKGROUND ) ) return fig # ============================================================ # EXPORT LOOP # ============================================================ ensure_kaleido() for step in STEP_DEFINITIONS: step_id = step["id"] step_dir = ROOT_EXPORT / step_id html_dir = step_dir / "HTML" png_dir = step_dir / "PNG" meta_dir = step_dir / "META" html_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) png_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) meta_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) fig = build_step_figure(step["layers"]) # ------------------------------------------------ # HTML # ------------------------------------------------ html_file = html_dir / (step_id + ".html") fig.write_html(str(html_file)) # ------------------------------------------------ # PNG EXPORTS # ------------------------------------------------ png_files=[] for view_name, view_data in VIEWS.items(): fig.update_layout( scene_camera=view_data["camera"] ) png_file = png_dir / ( step_id + "__" + view_name + ".png" ) fig.write_image( str(png_file), width=1100, height=650, scale=2 ) png_files.append(str(png_file)) # ------------------------------------------------ # META # ------------------------------------------------ meta = { "script_version": SCRIPT_VERSION, "step": step_id, "visible_layers": step["layers"], "counts": { "circles": len(circles), "points": len(points), "inner": len(inner), "level2": len(level2), "level3": len(level3), "outer": len(outer) }, "camera_views": list(VIEWS.keys()), "exports": { "html": str(html_file), "png": png_files } } json_file = meta_dir / (step_id + "_meta.json") with open( json_file, "w", encoding="utf-8" ) as f: json.dump( meta, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False ) csv_file = meta_dir / (step_id + "_points.csv") with open( csv_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8" ) as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow([ "x", "y", "z" ]) for p in points: writer.writerow([ float(p[0]), float(p[1]), float(p[2]) ]) # ============================================================ # OPEN FINAL HTML # ============================================================ final_html = ( ROOT_EXPORT / "STEP_3_XYZ_DIAGONALS" / "HTML" / "STEP_3_XYZ_DIAGONALS.html" ) webbrowser.open( "file://" + str(final_html.resolve()) ) print("") print("FULL EXPORT COMPLETE") print("") print("ROOT:", ROOT_EXPORT) print("") print("STEPS:") for step in STEP_DEFINITIONS: print(" -", step["id"]) ⚖️ — License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: SHEET 04
item.description: The Rx8 reconstruction establishes a continuous geometrical sequence beginning with a single invariant reference and progressing through successive layers of relational reconstruction.Rather than introducing independent mathematical objects, each stage is derived directly from the structural relation established before it.The reconstruction therefore preserves complete structural continuity from its geometrical origin to its computational representation.The complete reconstruction may be summarized as:Invariant Reference (R) ↓ Primary Geometrical Differentiation ↓ First Linear Encapsulation (R × 8) ↓ First Relational Differentiation (1/3 ↔ 2/3) ↓ First Fractal Representation (1/4 ↔ 3/4) ↓ Numerical Translation ↓ Recursive Propagation ↓ Machine Representation ↓ Relational Residual Every stage represents a successive reconstruction of the same invariant relational origin.The complete Rx8 reconstruction is established upon the following principles: Geometry precedes measurement. Relation precedes representation. Representation reconstructs relation. Numerical values express existing relations. Recursive propagation preserves structural identity. Residuals belong to representation rather than relation. Every reconstruction remains traceable to the original geometrical reference. No additional fundamental relation is introduced after the first geometrical differentiation. Within RP9, Rx8 establishes the geometrical foundation from which the subsequent verification architecture proceeds.Its operational role is to provide: the original geometrical reference, the first complete linear encapsulation, the first relational differentiation, the first representational framework, and the structural origin for K4, K5, and K6. Rx8 therefore functions as the geometrical calibration layer upon which the broader RP9 reconstruction is established.The complete methodological progression is:Geometry ↓ Relation ↓ Representation ↓ Verification ↓ Recursive Reconstruction Rx8 establishes the first three stages.K4, K5, and K6 extend the final two.Together they form one continuous reconstruction architecture.The purpose of Rx8 is not to introduce an isolated geometrical construction.Its purpose is to establish the invariant relational origin from which the complete RP9 verification architecture is reconstructed.Beginning with a single geometrical reference, the reconstruction proceeds through relational differentiation, representational translation, recursive verification, and structural propagation while preserving complete continuity with its original geometrical origin.Rx8 therefore serves as the geometrical foundation of the relational reconstruction developed throughout the RP9 framework. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

The declaration therefore functions as the formal bridge between verification and synthesis.Within the RP9 repository, S4 occupies the first presentation layer of C. RP9.
