item.title: A. METHODOLOGY
item.description: S1. META. The Fundamental Distinction between FORM ≠ STRUCTURE This is the methodology. It answers questions such as: - What is form? - What is structure? - Where does the first differentiation occur? - Why is Vesica not the first structure? - How does structure become extractable? - How do later structures develop recursively? It is thus a purely conceptual and derivational document. One of the most persistent sources of confusion in geometry is the tendency to treat form and structure as equivalent concepts.Within the RP9 framework, they are not equivalent.They represent two fundamentally different stages of relational development.A form is a continuous geometric whole.It may exist independently of established positional relations.A sphere, for example, possesses continuity, boundary and coherence without requiring an internal system of defined directions, intersection points or reusable positional references.A structure, by contrast, is not defined by continuity alone.A structure exists only when stable relational positions have become sufficiently established to permit the extraction, identification and repeated use of geometric relations.Structure therefore presupposes relation.Form does not.Accordingly, form and structure cannot be treated as interchangeable descriptions of the same geometric object.They belong to different methodological levels.The transition from form to structure is therefore not a change of appearance.It is the establishment of a new relational state.For this reason, RP9 begins with form rather than structure.The objective is not to assume that structural organisation already exists.The objective is to determine the minimal relational conditions required for structure to become possible.This distinction constitutes the methodological foundation for every subsequent stage presented throughout the First Differentiation framework.The transition from form to structure cannot begin through structure itself.It must begin through the establishment of the first relation.Within the RP9 framework, this first relation is not created by introducing a new geometric object.Instead, it arises when the original spherical form becomes capable of relating to itself.No change of radius occurs.No deformation of the original form is introduced.The only change is relational.Two equivalent spherical forms establish a stable self-relation while preserving complete geometric equivalence.The first observable consequence of this relation is not yet a structure.It is the emergence of a new form that was not previously available within the isolated sphere.This new form appears as the intersection generated by the established self-relation.The intersection therefore does not represent an independently constructed object.It is the first geometric consequence of an already established relation.Accordingly, the intersection circle is not introduced.It is derived.This derivation constitutes the first measurable differentiation within the RP9 framework.The differentiation does not arise because the original sphere changes.It arises because the established relation makes a previously unavailable form observable.The internal circle therefore represents the first relationally generated form.Its emergence establishes the primary relational invariant developed throughout the remainder of the framework.This newly established form now becomes available for the next recursive application of the H–D–R operator.Only when the derived internal circle subsequently enters relation with itself does the framework proceed toward the first explicit two-dimensional relational configuration.Within RP9, this configuration is identified as Vesica Piscis.The methodological sequence can therefore be expressed as:Potential ↓ Spherical Form ↓ Self Relation ↓ First Differentiation ↓ Intersection Form ↓ Internal Circle ↓ Second Self Relation ↓ Vesica Piscis Accordingly, Vesica Piscis is not the origin of the first differentiation.It is the first relational configuration generated from a form that has already undergone the first differentiation.The first differentiation establishes more than a new geometric form.It establishes the first invariant relational condition.Within the RP9 framework, an invariant is not defined as a numerical value.Nor is it defined as a particular geometric configuration.An invariant is a relational condition that remains preserved while compatible forms, representations and subsequent structures continue to develop.Accordingly, the first differentiation does not merely generate an internal circle.It establishes the first stable relational proportion from which every subsequent compatible construction derives.The resulting proportion is expressed through the complementary relation:These values should not be understood as the origin of the relation.They are the numerical representation of a relation that has already become established through the first differentiation.The relational condition therefore precedes its mathematical expression.The numerical values merely describe what the relation already is.For this reason, the primary invariant is not created through measurement.Measurement reproduces an invariant that already exists.The first differentiation therefore establishes a permanent relational reference.Every subsequent compatible form, geometric configuration and structural extraction remains traceable to this same invariant relation.The relational identity may subsequently be represented through different dimensions, coordinate systems, numerical encodings or computational approximations.These representations may vary.The underlying relational condition does not.Accordingly, the first relational invariant may be expressed as:First Differentiation ↓ Primary Relational Invariant ↓ Representation ↓ Projection ↓ Measurement The methodological sequence therefore proceeds from relation toward representation, never in the opposite direction.Every subsequent structural possibility introduced throughout the RP9 framework presupposes the continued existence of this invariant.No later structure replaces it.Each compatible structure preserves and extends the same relational foundation established through the first differentiation.Within the RP9 framework, Vesica Piscis should not be understood as the first completed structure.It represents the first stable relational configuration established between differentiated forms.Its significance therefore does not lie in the existence of the configuration itself.Its significance lies in what that configuration makes possible.The Vesica configuration consists of two related forms together with the relational field established between them.At this stage, relation has been established.Differentiation has already occurred.The primary relational invariant has already been preserved.However, the framework has not yet produced a complete structural system.A structure requires more than related forms.It requires stable positional references capable of defining reusable geometric relations.Within the Vesica configuration these references first become explicitly available.The two centre nodes establish the primary positional references.The intersection points establish additional positional references.Together they define the first set of stable locations from which linear geometric relations may be extracted.Accordingly, Vesica Piscis should not be understood as the completed structure.It should be understood as the relational configuration that makes explicit structure possible.The structural origin therefore lies not in the existence of the Vesica itself, but in the extraction of stable geometric relations from the positional references established within it.The methodological transition may therefore be expressed as:Differentiated Forms ↓ Vesica Piscis ↓ Centre Nodes + Intersection Nodes ↓ Linear Relations ↓ First Extractable 2D Structure The centres and intersection points together establish the first reusable positional system.From this point onward, lengths, directions and geometric connections may be identified, reproduced and recursively propagated.Only at this stage does the framework transition from relational configuration to explicit structural organisation.Vesica Piscis therefore functions as the relational bridge between form and structure.It is not the structure itself.It is the condition under which structure first becomes geometrically extractable.The transition from relational configuration to structure does not occur through the introduction of additional forms.It occurs through the emergence of stable positional references.Within the Vesica configuration, these references are established through the centres of the two related circles together with their corresponding intersection points.Each position exists because of the previously established relational configuration.None of them is introduced independently.Together they form the first stable positional system.Once these positions have become established, geometric relations may be extracted directly from them.Distances may be identified.Directions may be defined.Connections may be reproduced.The configuration therefore becomes more than a relation between forms.It becomes a relational framework capable of supporting explicit geometric organisation.Structure is therefore not created by adding new geometry.Structure is extracted from the positional information already contained within the relational configuration.The centres establish the primary reference nodes.The intersection points establish complementary reference nodes.The linear relations connecting these positions constitute the first explicit structural elements.Accordingly, the first structure is not the Vesica itself.The first structure is the network of reproducible geometric relations that becomes extractable from the Vesica configuration.The methodological transition may therefore be expressed as:Relational Configuration ↓ Stable Positional References ↓ Reference Nodes ↓ Linear Relations ↓ Extractable Structure The extraction process is entirely relational.No additional geometric assumptions are introduced.The structure is revealed through the positional consistency already established by the preceding relational configuration.From this point onward, every subsequent construction within the RP9 framework proceeds through the same methodological principle.Previously established structures become the relational basis from which new positional systems may be extracted.Structure therefore develops recursively.Each new structural level preserves the relational consistency established by the previous one while making additional geometric organisation possible.The First Differentiation does not represent a singular geometric event.It establishes the relational principle from which every subsequent compatible structure may be derived.Once the primary relational invariant has been established, no additional relational origin is required.Subsequent structures do not introduce new foundational principles.They transform, propagate and reorganize the relational condition that has already been established.Accordingly, every later geometric construction remains methodologically connected to the same original differentiation.The relational origin is therefore unique.The structural manifestations are multiple.Each recursive application of the H–D–R operator begins from a form that has already been established through the preceding relational sequence.That form enters a new self-relation.A new differentiation becomes observable.A new form emerges.The process then repeats.The recursive sequence may therefore be expressed as:Established Form ↓ Self Relation ↓ Differentiation ↓ Primary Relational Invariant ↓ New Form ↓ Recursive Propagation Every newly generated form preserves the relational consistency of the previous level while making additional structural organisation possible.The recursive process therefore produces increasing structural complexity without introducing additional relational foundations.Structure grows.The relational origin remains unchanged.For this reason, RP9 does not describe a sequence of independent geometric constructions.It describes the recursive propagation of a single relational principle through successive transformations.Every compatible structure therefore remains traceable to the same First Differentiation.The methodological direction is always identical.Relation precedes differentiation.Differentiation establishes invariant relation.Invariant relation generates form.Form becomes capable of entering new relation.The process then repeats recursively.The complete methodological sequence may therefore be summarized as:Potential ↓ Form ↓ Self Relation ↓ First Differentiation ↓ Primary Relational Invariant ↓ Relational Configuration ↓ Extractable Structure ↓ New Form ↓ Recursive Propagation Within the RP9 framework, structural development is therefore not understood as the accumulation of independent geometric constructions.It is understood as the recursive transformation of one continuously preserved relational origin.Every compatible structural level extends the same relational foundation established through the First Differentiation.For this reason, the First Differentiation is not merely the beginning of the sequence.It remains the methodological origin of the entire recursive framework.The first extractable structure represents more than an isolated geometric configuration.It establishes the initial structural framework from which subsequent compatible structures may be derived.Within the RP9 framework, this property is referred to as Latent Structural Capacity.Latent structural capacity does not imply that every later structure is already fully manifested within the initial configuration.Rather, it means that the relational conditions required for their emergence have already been established.Once the first extractable structure exists, the fundamental positional references remain available for further relational organization.No additional relational origin is required.Every subsequent compatible structure therefore develops by reorganizing and extending the positional framework already established through the first differentiation.The process is not one of introducing fundamentally new structural principles.It is one of progressively revealing structural possibilities that are already inherent within the existing relational framework.The methodological sequence may therefore be expressed as:First Extractable Structure ↓ Latent Structural Capacity ↓ Relational Reorganization ↓ New Structural Manifestation The emergence of later structures should therefore not be understood as independent geometric creation.Each new structural manifestation represents a further operational realization of relational possibilities that already exist within the original extractable structure.Accordingly, structural development is cumulative rather than discontinuous.Each successive level preserves the relational consistency of the previous one while expanding its observable structural organization.The original framework is therefore not replaced.It is progressively unfolded through recursive relational operations.Within this perspective, latent structural capacity represents the permanent structural potential established by the first extractable organization.Every subsequent compatible manifestation remains traceable to this same relational foundation.For this reason, the first extractable structure functions not merely as the beginning of a geometric sequence.It functions as the relational source from which all subsequent compatible structural developments become operationally possible.The latent structural capacity established by the first extractable structure does not become observable simultaneously.It becomes observable through a sequential process of relational manifestation.Each newly identifiable structure represents a further expression of the same underlying relational organization.No new relational foundation is introduced.The existing structural framework is progressively unfolded through successive relational transformations.Accordingly, the emergence of later structures should not be understood as the creation of independent geometric objects.Each structure becomes observable because the relational conditions required for its existence have already been established within the original structural framework.The process is therefore cumulative rather than additive.As the relational organization expands, additional structural properties become explicitly identifiable.These include successive manifestations such as: the equilateral triangle, the rhombic relation, the square, the balanced 45° orientation, the diagonal relation represented by , and the triangular relation represented by . Within the RP9 framework, these should not be interpreted as unrelated geometric discoveries.They represent successive manifestations of one continuously preserved relational origin.The methodological sequence may therefore be expressed as:First Extractable Structure ↓ Rhombic Bi-Rhomb ↓ Sequential Structural Manifestation ↓ Triangle ↓ Rhomb ↓ Square ↓ 45° 45° Relational Balance ↓ √2 ↓ √3 ↓ Recursive Structural Expansion This sequence does not describe independent geometric constructions.It describes the progressive disclosure of structural relations that were already latent within the first extractable organization.Each stage preserves the relational consistency established by the previous stage.Each stage simultaneously expands the observable structural capacity of the framework.Accordingly, structural development proceeds through relational continuity rather than discontinuous invention.Every newly observable relation remains traceable to the same original structural source.Within the RP9 framework, this source is represented by the first extractable structure.It constitutes the common relational origin from which all subsequent compatible structural manifestations are sequentially derived.For this reason, the apparent diversity of later geometric structures should not be understood as evidence of multiple independent origins.It reflects the progressive manifestation of one continuously preserved relational foundation.The sequential manifestation of structural organization does not require the introduction of new relational foundations.Every successive structural level develops through the recursive propagation of the same relational origin established by the first differentiation.Within the RP9 framework, recursive propagation does not represent the repeated creation of independent structures.It represents the continued operational realization of relations that are already latent within the original extractable framework.Each recursive operation begins from an existing structural organization.That organization enters a new relational configuration.Previously latent structural capacity becomes operationally explicit.New structural manifestations emerge.The underlying relational foundation, however, remains unchanged.The recursive process may therefore be expressed as:Existing Structure ↓ Recursive Relational Operation ↓ Latent Relations Become Explicit ↓ Expanded Structural Organization ↓ Recursive Continuity The recursive operator therefore performs no replacement of relational origin.Its function is to propagate an already established structural foundation through successive levels of relational organization.Structural complexity increases.Relational continuity remains invariant.Accordingly, recursive propagation should not be understood as the accumulation of unrelated geometric constructions.It is the progressive operational unfolding of one continuously preserved relational framework.Every newly manifested structure extends the observable organization of the system while remaining fully traceable to the same original structural source.The recursive operator therefore introduces no new relational principles.It reveals additional structural consequences that were already inherently contained within the latent structural capacity established by the first extractable structure.Within this perspective, structural development is neither discontinuous nor generative in the sense of creating new foundational relations.It is recursive.Each successive manifestation preserves the original relational framework while expanding its observable structural organization.The complete methodological sequence developed throughout this document may therefore be summarized as:Potential ↓ Form ↓ Self Relation ↓ First Differentiation ↓ Primary Relational Invariant ↓ Relational Configuration ↓ Extractable Structure ↓ Latent Structural Capacity ↓ Sequential Manifestation ↓ Recursive Structural Propagation Within the RP9 framework, this sequence represents a continuous methodological derivation.Each stage follows from the relational conditions established by the previous one.No additional relational origin is introduced.Every compatible structural manifestation remains recursively connected to the same foundational differentiation.For this reason, recursive structural propagation is not the conclusion of the framework.It is its general operational principle. item.title: README
item.description:
The RP9 Introduction serves as the conceptual and methodological entry point to the RP9 repository.Its purpose is to establish the context through which the remainder of the repository should be understood.Rather than introducing new relational derivations or verification results, this section defines the framework, explains the presentation architecture, establishes the methodological terminology, and prepares the reader for the sequential development presented throughout the repository.The introduction therefore functions as the foundation upon which the remaining repository is built.The Introduction has five primary functions: define the RP9 relational framework, present the repository's methodological architecture, explain how the repository is organized and intended to be read, establish the principles of reproducibility and traceability, formally declare the presentation architecture that governs the repository. Together these functions provide the conceptual foundation required before entering the primary methodological sequence.The RP9 repository is organized according to the following primary presentation architecture:0. item.title: SHEET 1 — WHAT IS RP9
item.description: SHEET 1 Function: Define the RP9 relational framework. RP9 is a relational framework for the sequential establishment, derivation, reproduction, verification, and formal declaration of invariant relational structures.Rather than describing isolated mathematical objects or independent representations, RP9 is founded upon the principle of relational primacy, where relational structure precedes geometry, mathematics, notation, and representation.RP9 therefore describes a coherent relational architecture through which structural relationships can be established, reproduced, examined, and documented in a traceable and reproducible manner.It is the framework that defines the methodology.The repository provides the primary presentation and verification environment through which that methodology is communicated.The primary function of RP9 is to establish an invariant relational structure from which all subsequent observations, reproductions, and applications are derived.Within this framework, RP9 performs five complementary functions: establish relational structures, derive those structures through a continuous relational sequence, reproduce the established structures through operational methods, verify their structural continuity, and formally document the complete derivation. These functions together constitute the methodological foundation of the framework.RP9 follows a sequential methodology in which every subsequent stage depends upon relationships established previously.The general order is:Relation ↓ Structure ↓ Derivation ↓ Reproduction ↓ Verification ↓ Documentation Each stage extends the previous one.No stage replaces an earlier stage.The continuity of the framework is therefore preserved throughout the complete derivation.RP9 separates the establishment of relational structure from its subsequent verification.Accordingly, the framework operates through two complementary methodological layers.The first establishes and derives the relational structure.The second reproduces, verifies, documents, and summarizes the established structure.This separation allows derivation and verification to be examined independently while preserving their continuous relational connection.A defining characteristic of RP9 is reproducibility.Every documented result should be traceable to the relational sequence through which it was established.Likewise, every reproduced result should correspond to the same documented relational structure.Documentation, computational implementation, and verification therefore constitute different methodological expressions of the same underlying framework.RP9 encompasses all methodological components required to establish and examine the relational framework, including: formal documentation, computational implementation, verification procedures, supporting data, summary documentation, and reference documentation. Each component performs a distinct methodological function while contributing to the same coherent relational framework.RP9 is a functional and relational framework for the sequential establishment, derivation, reproduction, verification, and documentation of invariant relational structures.It defines the methodology through which relational structures are established, reproduced, and formally examined.The repository organises this methodology into a coherent presentation and verification environment where every document, every code base, and every verification procedure performs one clearly defined function within a continuous relational architecture.Together they provide a traceable, reproducible, and methodologically consistent framework for the presentation and examination of RP9. Every architectural decision supports these objectives.The RP9 repository is organised as the primary presentation and verification environment of the RP9 relational framework.Its functional architecture separates presentation, calibration, verification, summarisation, and supporting documentation into distinct but continuous methodological layers.Each document contributes one clearly defined function.Together they establish a coherent, reproducible, traceable, and scalable presentation architecture through which the RP9 framework can be examined, reproduced, and formally declared. item.description: # ============================================================ # RP9_FORM_ONLY_HDR_PRESENTATION.py # # KORRIGERAD PROPORTION: # # Yttre metasfär: # radie = R # # Två inre sfärer: # radie = r # centrumavstånd = r # # För att båda inre sfärerna samtidigt ska: # 1. stå i halva-halva-relation, # 2. vara symmetriskt centrerade, # 3. tangera den yttre metasfären, # # gäller: # # R = r + r/2 # R = 3r/2 # r = 2R/3 # # Därmed: # centrum 1 = (-R/3, 0, 0) # centrum 2 = ( R/3, 0, 0) # centrumavstånd = 2R/3 = r # # Intersektionscirkelns radie: # # r_i = sqrt(r^2 - (r/2)^2) # = sqrt(3)/2 * r # = R/sqrt(3) # # Presentationen innehåller endast: # - grön metasfär # - blå inre sfär # - röd inre sfär # - vit intersektionscirkel # - vitt diameterstreck över intersektionscirkeln # # Inga mått, noder, axlar, kors, romber eller etiketter. # # Kräver: # pip install numpy plotly # ============================================================ from __future__ import annotations import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go # ============================================================ # PARAMETRAR # ============================================================ META_RADIUS = 3.0 SPHERE_RESOLUTION = 140 CIRCLE_RESOLUTION = 900 BACKGROUND_COLOR = "black" META_COLOR = "#00C853" BLUE_COLOR = "#087EA4" RED_COLOR = "#C0392B" WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" META_OPACITY = 0.20 INNER_OPACITY = 0.48 INTERSECTION_WIDTH = 8 DIAMETER_WIDTH = 6 AUTO_OPEN_HTML = True OUTPUT_METAPOTENTIAL = "01_METAPOTENTIAL_FORM.html" OUTPUT_HDR = "02_HDR_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_FORM.html" # ============================================================ # GEOMETRI # ============================================================ def create_sphere( center: np.ndarray, radius: float, resolution: int, ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: u = np.linspace(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, resolution) v = np.linspace(0.0, np.pi, resolution) x = radius * np.outer(np.cos(u), np.sin(v)) + center[0] y = radius * np.outer(np.sin(u), np.sin(v)) + center[1] z = radius * np.outer(np.ones_like(u), np.cos(v)) + center[2] return x, y, z def create_intersection_circle( center_1: np.ndarray, center_2: np.ndarray, sphere_radius: float, resolution: int, ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float]: center_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(center_2 - center_1)) if center_distance <= 0.0: raise ValueError("Centrumavståndet måste vara större än noll.") if center_distance >= 2.0 * sphere_radius: raise ValueError("Sfärerna överlappar inte.") midpoint = (center_1 + center_2) / 2.0 intersection_radius = np.sqrt( sphere_radius**2 - (center_distance / 2.0) ** 2 ) theta = np.linspace(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, resolution) # Sfärernas centrum ligger längs x-axeln. # Intersektionscirkeln ligger därför i planet x = 0. x = np.full_like(theta, midpoint[0]) y = midpoint[1] + intersection_radius * np.cos(theta) z = midpoint[2] + intersection_radius * np.sin(theta) points = np.vstack((x, y, z)) return points, float(intersection_radius) def constant_colorscale(color: str) -> list[list[object]]: return [[0.0, color], [1.0, color]] def sphere_trace( center: np.ndarray, radius: float, color: str, opacity: float, ) -> go.Surface: x, y, z = create_sphere( center=center, radius=radius, resolution=SPHERE_RESOLUTION, ) return go.Surface( x=x, y=y, z=z, surfacecolor=np.zeros_like(x), colorscale=constant_colorscale(color), cmin=0.0, cmax=1.0, opacity=opacity, showscale=False, hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False, lighting=dict( ambient=0.88, diffuse=0.58, specular=0.08, roughness=0.95, fresnel=0.02, ), lightposition=dict( x=100.0, y=100.0, z=100.0, ), ) # ============================================================ # LAYOUT # ============================================================ def form_only_layout(radius: float) -> dict: limit = radius * 1.08 hidden_axis = dict( visible=False, showgrid=False, showbackground=False, zeroline=False, showticklabels=False, title="", range=[-limit, limit], ) return dict( paper_bgcolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, plot_bgcolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=0, b=0), showlegend=False, scene=dict( bgcolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, xaxis=hidden_axis, yaxis=hidden_axis, zaxis=hidden_axis, aspectmode="cube", camera=dict( # Frontal startvy längs x-axeln. # Intersektionscirkeln visas då som en cirkel. eye=dict(x=2.45, y=0.0, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0), projection=dict(type="orthographic"), ), ), ) def export_html(fig: go.Figure, output_path: Path) -> None: fig.write_html( str(output_path), include_plotlyjs=True, full_html=True, auto_open=False, config={ "displayModeBar": False, "scrollZoom": True, "responsive": True, }, ) if AUTO_OPEN_HTML: webbrowser.open(output_path.resolve().as_uri()) # ============================================================ # 1. METAPOTENTIAL # ============================================================ def build_metapotential() -> go.Figure: center = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]) fig = go.Figure( data=[ sphere_trace( center=center, radius=META_RADIUS, color=META_COLOR, opacity=0.38, ) ] ) fig.update_layout(**form_only_layout(META_RADIUS)) return fig # ============================================================ # 2. H-D-R / FÖRSTA DIFFERENTIERINGENS FORM # ============================================================ def build_hdr_form() -> go.Figure: meta_center = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]) # Korrekt proportion: # r = 2R/3 inner_radius = (2.0 / 3.0) * META_RADIUS # Halva-halva-relation: # centrumavståndet mellan sfärerna är lika med deras radie. center_distance = inner_radius center_1 = np.array( [-center_distance / 2.0, 0.0, 0.0] ) center_2 = np.array( [center_distance / 2.0, 0.0, 0.0] ) # Kontroll: # vardera inre sfär ska tangera metasfärens yta. outer_extent_1 = abs(center_1[0]) + inner_radius outer_extent_2 = abs(center_2[0]) + inner_radius if not np.isclose(outer_extent_1, META_RADIUS): raise RuntimeError("Blå sfär följer inte metasfärens proportion.") if not np.isclose(outer_extent_2, META_RADIUS): raise RuntimeError("Röd sfär följer inte metasfärens proportion.") intersection, intersection_radius = create_intersection_circle( center_1=center_1, center_2=center_2, sphere_radius=inner_radius, resolution=CIRCLE_RESOLUTION, ) traces = [ sphere_trace( center=meta_center, radius=META_RADIUS, color=META_COLOR, opacity=META_OPACITY, ), sphere_trace( center=center_1, radius=inner_radius, color=BLUE_COLOR, opacity=INNER_OPACITY, ), sphere_trace( center=center_2, radius=inner_radius, color=RED_COLOR, opacity=INNER_OPACITY, ), go.Scatter3d( x=intersection[0], y=intersection[1], z=intersection[2], mode="lines", line=dict( color=WHITE_COLOR, width=INTERSECTION_WIDTH, ), hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False, ), ] fig = go.Figure(data=traces) fig.update_layout(**form_only_layout(META_RADIUS)) return fig # ============================================================ # KÖRNING # ============================================================ def main() -> None: script_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent metapotential_path = script_dir / OUTPUT_METAPOTENTIAL hdr_path = script_dir / OUTPUT_HDR export_html( build_metapotential(), metapotential_path, ) export_html( build_hdr_form(), hdr_path, ) print("") print("KLART") print("") print("Korrekt proportion:") print(f"Metasfärens radie: {META_RADIUS}") print( "Inre sfärernas radie: " f"{(2.0 / 3.0) * META_RADIUS}" ) print( "Centrumavstånd: " f"{(2.0 / 3.0) * META_RADIUS}" ) print( "Intersektionscirkelns radie: " f"{META_RADIUS / np.sqrt(3.0)}" ) print("") print(f"1. {metapotential_path}") print(f"2. {hdr_path}") print("") if __name__ == "__main__": main()

item.title: C. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION.REVISED. PYTHON
item.description: # RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED.py # Version: 2.0.0 # Purpose: # - Explicitly isolates form differentiation before structural emergence. # - Verifies one sphere -> two equivalent spheres -> half-half position. # - Derives the first common intersection circle. # - Verifies the exact 3/4 and 1/4 relation. # - Separates exact geometry, RP9 interpretation and float representation. from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime import hashlib import json import math import platform import sys import traceback from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass from decimal import Decimal, getcontext from fractions import Fraction from pathlib import Path from typing import Any getcontext().prec = 80 SCRIPT_NAME = "RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED.py" SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.0" OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED" # ============================================================ # GENERAL UTILITIES # ============================================================ def now_local() -> str: return datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") def now_utc_iso() -> str: return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace( microsecond=0 ).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z") def script_dir() -> Path: try: return Path(__file__).resolve().parent except NameError: return Path.cwd().resolve() BASE_DIR = script_dir() OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / OUTPUT_DIR_NAME def ensure_output_dir() -> None: OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def sci(value: float, digits: int = 20) -> str: return format(float(value), f".{digits}e") def decimal_from_fraction(value: Fraction, places: int = 20) -> str: d = Decimal(value.numerator) / Decimal(value.denominator) return format(d, f".{places}f") def json_safe(obj: Any) -> Any: if isinstance(obj, dict): return {str(k): json_safe(v) for k, v in obj.items()} if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)): return [json_safe(v) for v in obj] if isinstance(obj, Path): return str(obj) if isinstance(obj, Fraction): return str(obj) if isinstance(obj, Decimal): return str(obj) if hasattr(obj, "__dataclass_fields__"): return json_safe(asdict(obj)) if isinstance(obj, (str, int, float, bool)) or obj is None: return obj return str(obj) def write_text(path: Path, lines: list[str]) -> None: path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") def write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None: path.write_text( json.dumps(json_safe(payload), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8", ) def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256() with path.open("rb") as f: while True: chunk = f.read(1024 * 1024) if not chunk: break h.update(chunk) return h.hexdigest() def distance_3d(a: "Point3D", b: "Point3D") -> Fraction: dx = b.x - a.x dy = b.y - a.y dz = b.z - a.z squared = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz if squared.denominator == 1: root = math.isqrt(squared.numerator) if root * root == squared.numerator: return Fraction(root, 1) return Fraction.from_float(math.sqrt(float(squared))) def make_trace( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], layer: str, operation: str, formula: str, inputs: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any], status: str, note: str, ) -> None: trace.append( { "index": len(trace) + 1, "timestamp_utc": now_utc_iso(), "layer": layer, "operation": operation, "formula": formula, "inputs": json_safe(inputs), "result": json_safe(result), "status": status, "note": note, } ) # ============================================================ # GEOMETRIC DATA TYPES # ============================================================ @dataclass(frozen=True) class Point3D: x: Fraction y: Fraction z: Fraction def as_tuple(self) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]: return self.x, self.y, self.z @dataclass(frozen=True) class Sphere: center: Point3D radius: Fraction @dataclass(frozen=True) class IntersectionCircle: center: Point3D normal_axis: str radius_squared: Fraction radius_symbolic: str # ============================================================ # A. META-POTENTIAL # ============================================================ def compute_meta_potential(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "A_META_POTENTIAL" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) sphere = Sphere(center=center, radius=radius) form_count = 1 center_count = 1 passed = ( form_count == 1 and center_count == 1 and sphere.radius == Fraction(1, 1) ) make_trace( trace, layer, "define_single_spherical_form", "P0 = Sphere(C0, R)", {}, { "sphere": sphere, "form_count": form_count, "center_count": center_count, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Defines one spherical form as the pre-structural geometric reference.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Defines one spherical form before internal relational structure.", "geometry": { "form_count": form_count, "center_count": center_count, "center": center, "radius": radius, }, "classification": { "form_status": "SINGLE_SPHERICAL_FORM", "structural_status": "PRE_STRUCTURAL", "rp9_interpretation": "META_POTENTIAL", }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # B. SELF-RELATION # ============================================================ def compute_self_relation(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "B_SELF_RELATION" radius_1 = Fraction(1, 1) radius_2 = Fraction(1, 1) equal_radii = radius_1 == radius_2 no_new_scale = equal_radii initial_form_count = 1 relational_form_count = 2 passed = ( equal_radii and no_new_scale and initial_form_count == 1 and relational_form_count == 2 ) make_trace( trace, layer, "reproduce_equivalent_form", "R1 = R2 = R", {"R1": radius_1}, { "R2": radius_2, "equal_radii": equal_radii, "initial_form_count": initial_form_count, "relational_form_count": relational_form_count, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Reproduces the same spherical form without introducing a new scale.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Reproduces the spherical reference as an equivalent self-relation.", "form_transition": { "before": initial_form_count, "after": relational_form_count, }, "radius_relation": { "R1": radius_1, "R2": radius_2, "equal_radii": equal_radii, "new_scale_introduced": not no_new_scale, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # C. FIRST FORM DIFFERENTIATION # ============================================================ def compute_first_form_differentiation( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "C_FIRST_FORM_DIFFERENTIATION" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) sphere_1 = Sphere(center=center_1, radius=radius) sphere_2 = Sphere(center=center_2, radius=radius) form_count_before = 1 form_count_after = 2 equal_form = sphere_1.radius == sphere_2.radius distinct_centers = sphere_1.center != sphere_2.center differentiation_exists = ( form_count_before == 1 and form_count_after == 2 and equal_form and distinct_centers ) make_trace( trace, layer, "differentiate_form_by_position", "1 equivalent form -> 2 equivalent forms with C1 != C2", {"form_count_before": form_count_before}, { "form_count_after": form_count_after, "sphere_1": sphere_1, "sphere_2": sphere_2, "equal_form": equal_form, "distinct_centers": distinct_centers, }, "PASS" if differentiation_exists else "FAIL", "Isolates the first differentiation before intersection structure.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the transition from one form to two equivalent forms.", "forms": { "sphere_1": sphere_1, "sphere_2": sphere_2, "form_count_before": form_count_before, "form_count_after": form_count_after, "equal_form": equal_form, "distinct_centers": distinct_centers, }, "classification": { "difference_source": "POSITION", "structure_required": False, "differentiation": "FORM_DIFFERENTIATION_CONFIRMED" if differentiation_exists else "FORM_DIFFERENTIATION_FAILED", }, "status": "PASS" if differentiation_exists else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # D. HALF-HALF POSITIONAL LOCK # ============================================================ def compute_half_half_lock(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "D_HALF_HALF_POSITIONAL_LOCK" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint = Point3D( (center_1.x + center_2.x) / 2, (center_1.y + center_2.y) / 2, (center_1.z + center_2.z) / 2, ) center_distance = distance_3d(center_1, center_2) expected_midpoint = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint_valid = midpoint == expected_midpoint distance_valid = center_distance == radius half_half_valid = ( center_1.x == -radius / 2 and center_2.x == radius / 2 and midpoint_valid and distance_valid ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_half_half_position", "C1 = -R/2 ; C2 = +R/2 ; |C2-C1| = R", {"R": radius}, { "C1": center_1, "C2": center_2, "midpoint": midpoint, "center_distance": center_distance, }, "PASS" if half_half_valid else "FAIL", "Locks the two differentiated forms symmetrically around one midpoint.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the symmetric half-half positional relation.", "position": { "R": radius, "C1": center_1, "C2": center_2, "midpoint": midpoint, "center_distance": center_distance, }, "verification": { "midpoint_is_origin": midpoint_valid, "center_distance_equals_radius": distance_valid, "half_half_position_valid": half_half_valid, }, "status": "PASS" if half_half_valid else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # E. FIRST STRUCTURAL INTERSECTION # ============================================================ def compute_first_intersection(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "E_FIRST_STRUCTURAL_INTERSECTION" radius = Fraction(1, 1) distance = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) intersection_exists = ( distance > 0 and distance < 2 * radius ) ri_squared = radius * radius - (distance / 2) * (distance / 2) ri_float = math.sqrt(float(ri_squared)) radius_float = float(radius) intersection_radius_smaller = ri_float < radius_float circle = IntersectionCircle( center=midpoint, normal_axis="x", radius_squared=ri_squared, radius_symbolic="sqrt(3)/2 * R", ) passed = ( intersection_exists and ri_squared == Fraction(3, 4) and intersection_radius_smaller ) make_trace( trace, layer, "derive_intersection_circle", "ri^2 = R^2 - (D/2)^2", {"R": radius, "D": distance}, { "intersection_circle": circle, "ri_squared": ri_squared, "ri_float": ri_float, "intersection_radius_smaller": intersection_radius_smaller, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Derives the first common relational structure after form differentiation.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Derives the first common intersection structure.", "intersection": { "exists": intersection_exists, "plane_center": midpoint, "plane_normal_axis": "x", "radius_squared_exact": ri_squared, "radius_symbolic": "sqrt(3)/2 * R", "radius_float": sci(ri_float), "sphere_radius_float": sci(radius_float), "intersection_radius_is_smaller": intersection_radius_smaller, }, "classification": { "rp9_name": "VESICA_PISCIS", "structural_status": "FIRST_RELATIONAL_STRUCTURE", "preceded_by_form_differentiation": True, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # F. EXACT RELATIONAL RESULT # ============================================================ def compute_exact_relational_result( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "F_EXACT_RELATIONAL_RESULT" radius_squared = Fraction(1, 1) intersection_radius_squared = Fraction(3, 4) ratio_exact = intersection_radius_squared / radius_squared lock_exact = Fraction(1, 1) - ratio_exact ratio_float = float(ratio_exact) lock_float = float(lock_exact) ratio_float_residual = Fraction.from_float(ratio_float) - ratio_exact lock_float_residual = Fraction.from_float(lock_float) - lock_exact passed = ( ratio_exact == Fraction(3, 4) and lock_exact == Fraction(1, 4) and ratio_float_residual == 0 and lock_float_residual == 0 ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_exact_ratio_and_lock", "ri^2/R^2 = 3/4 ; 1 - 3/4 = 1/4", { "ri_squared": intersection_radius_squared, "R_squared": radius_squared, }, { "ratio_exact": ratio_exact, "lock_exact": lock_exact, "ratio_float_residual": ratio_float_residual, "lock_float_residual": lock_float_residual, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Verifies the exact relation after the full geometric derivation.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the exact 3/4 and 1/4 relation.", "exact_geometry": { "intersection_radius_squared": intersection_radius_squared, "sphere_radius_squared": radius_squared, "ratio_exact": ratio_exact, "complementary_lock_exact": lock_exact, }, "decimal_rendering": { "ratio_20_places": decimal_from_fraction(ratio_exact, 20), "lock_20_places": decimal_from_fraction(lock_exact, 20), }, "float_conversion": { "ratio_float": ratio_float, "lock_float": lock_float, "ratio_residual_against_exact": ratio_float_residual, "lock_residual_against_exact": lock_float_residual, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # G. REPRESENTATION CONTROL # ============================================================ def compute_representation_control( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "G_REPRESENTATION_CONTROL" radius = 1.0 distance = 1.0 ri = math.sqrt(radius * radius - (distance / 2.0) ** 2) area_y = math.pi * radius * radius area_i = math.pi * ri * ri ratio = area_i / area_y lock = 1.0 - ratio ratio_expected = 0.75 lock_expected = 0.25 ratio_residual = ratio - ratio_expected lock_residual = lock - lock_expected symmetric_residual = abs(ratio_residual + lock_residual) <= 1e-30 ratio_is_lower = ratio < ratio_expected lock_is_higher = lock > lock_expected epsilon = sys.float_info.epsilon next_value = math.nextafter(1.0, 2.0) next_diff = next_value - 1.0 passed = ( symmetric_residual and ratio_is_lower and lock_is_higher and next_diff == epsilon ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_float_rendering", "ratio=(pi*ri^2)/(pi*R^2) ; lock=1-ratio", {"R": radius, "D": distance}, { "ratio": ratio, "lock": lock, "ratio_residual": ratio_residual, "lock_residual": lock_residual, "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual, }, "PASS" if passed else "REVIEW", "Confirms representation behaviour separately from exact geometry.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Separates binary float rendering from exact geometry.", "float_geometry": { "R": sci(radius), "D": sci(distance), "ri": sci(ri), "AY": sci(area_y), "AI": sci(area_i), }, "float_lock": { "ratio_observed": sci(ratio), "ratio_expected": sci(ratio_expected), "ratio_residual": sci(ratio_residual), "ratio_hex": ratio.hex(), "lock_observed": sci(lock), "lock_expected": sci(lock_expected), "lock_residual": sci(lock_residual), "lock_hex": lock.hex(), }, "machine_precision": { "epsilon": sci(epsilon), "nextafter_1_to_2": sci(next_value), "nextafter_diff": sci(next_diff), "nextafter_matches_epsilon": next_diff == epsilon, }, "classification": { "ratio_is_lower_than_0_75": ratio_is_lower, "lock_is_higher_than_0_25": lock_is_higher, "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual, "exact_geometry_affected": False, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "REVIEW", } # ============================================================ # H. MASTER CONCLUSION # ============================================================ def build_master_conclusion( layers: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] ) -> dict[str, Any]: statuses = [layer["status"] for layer in layers.values()] if any(status == "FAIL" for status in statuses): total_status = "FAIL" elif any(status == "REVIEW" for status in statuses): total_status = "PASS_WITH_REVIEW_NOTES" else: total_status = "PASS" return { "layer_name": "H_MASTER_CONCLUSION", "chain": [ "META-POTENTIAL", "SINGLE SPHERICAL FORM", "SELF-RELATION", "TWO EQUIVALENT FORMS", "FIRST FORM DIFFERENTIATION", "HALF-HALF POSITION", "INTERSECTION", "VESICA PISCIS", "FIRST RELATIONAL STRUCTURE", "EXACT 3/4 RELATION", "COMPLEMENTARY 1/4 LOCK", "REPRESENTATION CONTROL", ], "summary": { key: value["status"] for key, value in layers.items() }, "total_status": total_status, "measurement_boundary": ( "The code verifies geometric form count, center count, radius " "invariance, positional differentiation, half-half symmetry, " "intersection geometry, exact ratio and machine representation. " "RP9 interpretation remains explicitly separated." ), "rp9_interpretation_layer": { "separated_from_measurement": True, "interpretation": ( "FIRST DIFFERENTIATION is the transition from one spherical " "form to two equivalent spherical forms in distinct symmetric " "positions. Vesica Piscis is the first relational structure " "enabled by that prior differentiation." ), }, } # ============================================================ # RUN # ============================================================ def run_all() -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]: trace: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] layers = { "A_meta_potential": compute_meta_potential(trace), "B_self_relation": compute_self_relation(trace), "C_first_form_differentiation": compute_first_form_differentiation(trace), "D_half_half_positional_lock": compute_half_half_lock(trace), "E_first_structural_intersection": compute_first_intersection(trace), "F_exact_relational_result": compute_exact_relational_result(trace), "G_representation_control": compute_representation_control(trace), } master = build_master_conclusion(layers) payload = { "script": { "name": SCRIPT_NAME, "version": SCRIPT_VERSION, "created_at_local": now_local(), "created_at_utc": now_utc_iso(), "python_version": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(), "working_directory": str(BASE_DIR), "output_directory": str(OUTPUT_DIR), "purpose": ( "Complete verification of RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION from " "single form to relational structure." ), }, "layers": layers, "master_conclusion": master, } return payload, trace # ============================================================ # OUTPUT BUILDERS # ============================================================ def build_markdown( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> list[str]: layers = payload["layers"] master = payload["master_conclusion"] lines: list[str] = [] lines.extend( [ "# RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED", "", "## Control Chain", "", "```text", *master["chain"], "```", "", "## Layer Status", "", "| Layer | Status |", "|---|---|", ] ) for key, layer in layers.items(): lines.append(f"| {key} | `{layer['status']}` |") lines.extend( [ "", f"**Total status:** `{master['total_status']}`", "", "## Foundational Conclusion", "", master["rp9_interpretation_layer"]["interpretation"], "", "## Measurement Boundary", "", master["measurement_boundary"], "", "## Trace", "", "| Index | Layer | Operation | Status |", "|---|---|---|---|", ] ) for row in trace: lines.append( f"| {row['index']} | {row['layer']} | " f"{row['operation']} | `{row['status']}` |" ) return lines def build_control_log( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> list[str]: lines = [ "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED CONTROL LOG", "=" * 72, f"Created local: {payload['script']['created_at_local']}", f"Created UTC: {payload['script']['created_at_utc']}", f"Script: {payload['script']['name']}", f"Version: {payload['script']['version']}", "", "VERIFIED CHAIN", "-" * 72, ] for item in payload["master_conclusion"]["chain"]: lines.append(item) lines.extend(["", "TRACE", "-" * 72]) for row in trace: lines.extend( [ f"STEP {str(row['index']).zfill(3)}", f"Layer: {row['layer']}", f"Operation: {row['operation']}", f"Formula: {row['formula']}", f"Status: {row['status']}", f"Note: {row['note']}", "", ] ) lines.extend( [ "FINAL STATUS", "-" * 72, payload["master_conclusion"]["total_status"], "", "BOUNDARY", "-" * 72, payload["master_conclusion"]["measurement_boundary"], ] ) return lines def write_outputs( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Path]: ensure_output_dir() paths = { "data_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_DATA.json", "trace_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_TRACE.json", "full_datasheet_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_FULL_DATASHEET.json", "presentation_markdown": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_PRESENTATION.md", "control_log": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_CONTROL_LOG.txt", "verify_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_VERIFY.json", } write_json(paths["data_json"], payload) write_json(paths["trace_json"], trace) write_json( paths["full_datasheet_json"], {"payload": payload, "trace": trace}, ) write_text( paths["presentation_markdown"], build_markdown(payload, trace), ) write_text( paths["control_log"], build_control_log(payload, trace), ) verify_files = {} for name, path in paths.items(): if name == "verify_json": continue verify_files[name] = { "path": str(path), "bytes": path.stat().st_size, "sha256": sha256_file(path), } write_json( paths["verify_json"], { "script_name": SCRIPT_NAME, "script_version": SCRIPT_VERSION, "generated_at_utc": now_utc_iso(), "files": verify_files, }, ) return paths def print_summary( payload: dict[str, Any], paths: dict[str, Path], ) -> None: print("") print("=" * 72) print("RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED") print("=" * 72) for key, layer in payload["layers"].items(): print(f"{key}: {layer['status']}") print("-" * 72) print("total_status:", payload["master_conclusion"]["total_status"]) print("-" * 72) for name, path in paths.items(): print(f"{name}: {path}") print("=" * 72) print("") def generate_once() -> tuple[ dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Path], ]: payload, trace = run_all() paths = write_outputs(payload, trace) print_summary(payload, paths) return payload, trace, paths def write_error_log(exc: Exception) -> Path: ensure_output_dir() path = OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_ERROR.log" lines = [ "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED ERROR LOG", "=" * 72, f"Timestamp local: {now_local()}", f"Timestamp UTC: {now_utc_iso()}", f"Error type: {type(exc).__name__}", f"Error message: {exc}", "", "TRACEBACK", "-" * 72, *traceback.format_exc().splitlines(), ] write_text(path, lines) return path def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser( description=( "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION revised all-inclusive verifier." ) ) parser.add_argument( "--run-once", action="store_true", help="Generate all verification files and exit.", ) return parser.parse_args() def main() -> None: parse_args() try: generate_once() except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Execution interrupted by user.") except Exception as exc: error_path = write_error_log(exc) print("ERROR:", exc) print("Error log written to:", error_path) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ⚖️ item.title: B. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION. PRESENTATION — REVISED
item.description: This document presents the verified transition from an undifferentiated spherical form to the first relational structure.The sequence is intentionally divided into two primary stages:FORM DIFFERENTIATION and:STRUCTURAL EMERGENCE The first stage establishes the transition from one form to two forms.The second stage establishes the common structure generated when those differentiated forms intersect.META-POTENTIAL ↓ SINGLE FORM ↓ SELF-RELATION ↓ TWO EQUIVALENT FORMS ↓ FIRST DIFFERENTIATION ↓ HALF–HALF POSITION ↓ INTERSECTION ↓ VESICA PISCIS ↓ FIRST STRUCTURE ↓ 3/4 ↔ 1/4 ↓ REPRESENTATION CONTROL The initial sphere functions as the first geometrically measurable potential form.It is a form without established internal relational structure.The same spherical reference is reproduced:The transition:1 form ↓ 2 equivalent forms constitutes the first differentiation.The difference arises through position, not through a change in radius or form type.The two forms are equivalent in geometry but differentiated in location.This produces:equivalent form + distinct position = first differentiation The differentiation is therefore present before the intersection circle is calculated.Vesica Piscis is not yet required for the existence of this difference.The centers are positioned symmetrically:The midpoint is:and:The relation is locked as:−R/2 ↔ +R/2 The common intersection plane passes through the midpoint.The intersection-circle radius is derived from:therefore:With :and:The direct linear differentiation is:Since:the intersection circle is smaller than the generating spherical reference.This is the first measurable geometric consequence of the established form relation.Vesica Piscis is classified as:the first common relational structure generated by two already differentiated forms The sequence is therefore:Differentiation ↓ Relation ↓ Intersection ↓ Structure not:Vesica Piscis ↓ Differentiation This distinction is foundational for all subsequent RP9 modules.The area relation is:Therefore:The complementary relation is:The exact geometric relation is verified independently from floating-point rendering.The machine representation layer may display:and:These residuals belong to the representation layer.They do not alter the exact relational result:K1. 1. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION establishes the complete foundational sequence:Meta-Potential ↓ One Spherical Form ↓ Self-Relation ↓ Two Equivalent Spherical Forms ↓ First Differentiation Through Position ↓ Half–Half Relation ↓ Common Intersection ↓ Vesica Piscis ↓ First Relational Structure ↓ 3/4 ↔ 1/4 The first differentiation is therefore derived from form before structure.The first structure is subsequently generated through the active relation between the differentiated forms.This distinction is now isolated, measured, specified, and locked as the operational foundation of the remaining RP9 verification architecture.⚖️ — License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for full terms.

B. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION. PRESENTATION — REVISED Link — 🔗. B. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION. PRESENTATION — REVISED PYTHON Link — 🔗.
C. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION.REVISED. PYTHON RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION establishes and verifies the first relational differentiation generated from geometric form.The module does not begin with Vesica Piscis as an already completed structure.It begins with the pre-structural geometric condition from which Vesica Piscis can subsequently emerge.The verification chain is therefore:Meta-Potential ↓ Single Spherical Form ↓ Self-Relation ↓ Two Equivalent Spherical Forms ↓ First Differentiation Through Form ↓ Half–Half Positional Relation ↓ Intersection ↓ Vesica Piscis ↓ First Relational Structure The primary function of this module is to isolate the transition:One Form ↓ Two Forms before any structural intersection is introduced.This establishes the first differentiation as a consequence of form and position rather than as a consequence of an already completed structure.The module separates:FORM DIFFERENTIATION from:STRUCTURAL EMERGENCE Form differentiation occurs when one spherical reference is reproduced as two equivalent spherical forms with distinct centers.The forms remain equivalent in radius, but they are no longer identical in position.The first difference is therefore:same form + different position Structure emerges only when the two differentiated forms enter an active common relation through intersection.The intersection circle is therefore not the first differentiation itself.It is the first relational structure made possible by the preceding differentiation.The code verifies the following layers:A. Meta-Potential B. Self-Relation C. First Form Differentiation D. Half–Half Positional Lock E. First Structural Intersection F. Exact Relational Result G. Representation Control H. Master Conclusion The initial condition is represented by one spherical form:Sphere count = 1 Center count = 1 Radius = R This condition is treated as pre-structural.The sphere is geometrically measurable as form, but no internal relational structure has yet been generated.The initial spherical reference is reproduced without changing its radius:R₁ = R₂ = R The second form is not introduced as an unrelated external object.It is introduced as an equivalent self-reference.This produces:Sphere count: 1 → 2 Center count: 1 → 2 The first differentiation is thereby established.The two centers are positioned symmetrically around a common midpoint:The center distance is therefore:and the midpoint is:This locks the relation as:−R/2 ↔ +R/2 The half–half relation is established before the intersection structure is evaluated.Once the two differentiated forms occupy the locked relation:their common intersection plane is located at the midpoint.The radius of the intersection circle is:With :and therefore:The intersection circle is the first common relational structure.Within this module, Vesica Piscis is therefore classified as:the first structure enabled by the first differentiation and not as:the first differentiation itself The code verifies:and:The relation:3/4 ↔ 1/4 is therefore derived only after:one form → two forms → half–half position → intersection has been explicitly established.The module verifies:single_form_count = 1 dual_form_count = 2 equal_radii = true distinct_centers = true midpoint_is_origin = true center_distance_equals_radius = true half_half_position_valid = true intersection_exists = true intersection_radius_is_smaller = true intersection_radius_squared_ratio = 3/4 complementary_lock = 1/4 These conditions isolate the complete first differentiation chain.The measurement verifies: form count, center count, radius invariance, positional differentiation, half–half symmetry, center distance, intersection existence, intersection radius, exact ratio, complementary lock, machine representation. The RP9 interpretation is kept separate from the numerical measurement.The code does not claim that a Python object creates metaphysical potential.It verifies the geometric and numerical conditions through which RP9 represents the transition from potential form to relational structure.K1 establishes the foundational chain:Potential ↓ Form ↓ Differentiation ↓ Relation ↓ Structure All later K-series modules depend on this distinction.K2 and K3 may therefore assume that:differentiation precedes structure and that:structure emerges only when differentiated forms enter an active common relation K1. 1. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION passes only if all primary conditions are verified:FORM DIFFERENTIATION = PASS HALF–HALF POSITION = PASS INTERSECTION STRUCTURE = PASS EXACT 3/4 RELATION = PASS COMPLEMENTARY 1/4 LOCK = PASS REPRESENTATION CONTROL = PASS The module then serves as the point of origin for all later RP9 verification layers.⚖️ — License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for full terms.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 from __future__ import annotations import argparse, datetime as dt, hashlib, json, math, platform, sys from fractions import Fraction from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from matplotlib.patches import Circle, FancyBboxPatch from matplotlib.lines import Line2D SCRIPT_NAME='RP9_K1_P0_Cb_MEASUREMENT.py'; VERSION='1.0.0' R_EXACT=Fraction(1,1); D_EXACT=Fraction(1,1) RI2_EXACT=R_EXACT**2-(D_EXACT/2)**2 RATIO_EXACT=RI2_EXACT/R_EXACT**2; LOCK_EXACT=1-RATIO_EXACT R=float(R_EXACT); D=float(D_EXACT) RI=math.sqrt(R*R-(D/2)**2); DR=R-RI AY=math.pi*R*R; AI=math.pi*RI*RI FLOAT_RATIO=AI/AY; FLOAT_LOCK=1-FLOAT_RATIO RRES=FLOAT_RATIO-float(RATIO_EXACT); LRES=FLOAT_LOCK-float(LOCK_EXACT) def utc_now(): return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z') def frac(v): return f'{v.numerator}/{v.denominator}' def sha256(p): h=hashlib.sha256() with p.open('rb') as f: for c in iter(lambda:f.read(1048576),b''): h.update(c) return h.hexdigest() def datasheet(): lp=RI/R*100; dp=DR/R*100 tests={ 'R_positive':R>0,'D_positive':D>0,'self_relation_D_equals_R':D_EXACT==R_EXACT, 'ri_squared_exact_3_over_4':RI2_EXACT==Fraction(3,4),'ri_smaller_than_R':RI<R, 'area_ratio_exact_3_over_4':RATIO_EXACT==Fraction(3,4),'lock_exact_1_over_4':LOCK_EXACT==Fraction(1,4), 'linear_percent_sum_100':math.isclose(lp+dp,100,abs_tol=1e-12), 'area_percent_sum_100':math.isclose(float(RATIO_EXACT+LOCK_EXACT)*100,100,abs_tol=1e-12), 'float_residuals_symmetric':math.isclose(RRES+LRES,0,abs_tol=1e-30)} return { 'id':'K1_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_P0_C-b','name':'First Differentiation — Isolated Self-Relational Section', 'version':VERSION,'generated_at_utc':utc_now(),'units':'dimensionless', 'methodological_position':{'stage':'before explicit two-sphere Vesica Piscis presentation','classification':'isolated self-relational form measurement','relation':'D = R'}, 'input':{'R_exact':frac(R_EXACT),'D_exact':frac(D_EXACT),'R_float':R,'D_float':D}, 'derived_geometry':{'ri_formula':'sqrt(R^2 - (D/2)^2)','ri_symbolic':'sqrt(3)/2 * R','ri_squared_exact':frac(RI2_EXACT),'ri_float':RI,'delta_r':DR}, 'linear_relation':{'ri_over_R':RI/R,'ri_over_R_percent':lp,'delta_r_over_R':DR/R,'delta_r_over_R_percent':dp}, 'area_relation':{'ri_squared_over_R_squared_exact':frac(RATIO_EXACT),'AI_over_AY_exact':frac(RATIO_EXACT),'inner_percent':75.0,'differential_exact':frac(LOCK_EXACT),'differential_percent':25.0}, 'numerical_representation':{'exact_ratio':0.75,'exact_lock':0.25,'geometric_float_ratio':FLOAT_RATIO,'geometric_float_lock':FLOAT_LOCK,'ratio_residual':RRES,'lock_residual':LRES,'ratio_hex':FLOAT_RATIO.hex(),'lock_hex':FLOAT_LOCK.hex()}, 'verification':{'tests':tests,'total_status':'PASS' if all(tests.values()) else 'FAIL'}} def panel(ax,x,y,w,h,title,lines): ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x,y),w,h,boxstyle='round,pad=0.012,rounding_size=0.012',lw=1,ec=(1,1,1,.3),fc=(.03,.03,.03,.88),transform=ax.transAxes)) ax.text(x+.02,y+h-.035,title,transform=ax.transAxes,color='white',fontsize=11,fontweight='bold',va='top') yy=y+h-.09 for t,c,s in lines: ax.text(x+.02,yy,t,transform=ax.transAxes,color=c,fontsize=s,va='top',family='DejaVu Sans Mono'); yy-=.085 def make_png(path,dpi=180): fig=plt.figure(figsize=(16,9),facecolor='black') ax=fig.add_axes([.04,.30,.56,.62]); ax.set_facecolor('black'); ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.set_xlim(-1.3,1.9); ax.set_ylim(-1.15,1.15); ax.axis('off') outer='#7f0f2f'; inner='#7c2d63'; cyan='#22d3ee'; yellow='#fde047'; white='#f8fafc'; center='#fbcfe8' ax.add_patch(Circle((0,0),R,fc=outer,ec='#9f1239',lw=2.2,alpha=.92)) ax.add_patch(Circle((0,0),RI,fc=inner,ec=cyan,lw=2.8,alpha=.78)); ax.scatter([0],[0],s=58,color=center,zorder=8) ax.add_line(Line2D([0,0],[0,R],color=white,lw=2.2)); ax.add_line(Line2D([0,0],[0,-RI],color=cyan,lw=2.2)) ax.scatter([0,0],[R,-RI],s=34,color=[white,cyan],zorder=8); ax.text(.08,.50,'R',color=white,fontsize=24,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(.08,-.43,r'$r_i$',color=cyan,fontsize=24,fontweight='bold') ax.plot([-R,-RI],[0,0],color=yellow,lw=3); ax.plot([-R,-R],[-.06,.06],color=yellow,lw=2); ax.plot([-RI,-RI],[-.06,.06],color=yellow,lw=2) ax.annotate('',xy=(-RI,.14),xytext=(-R,.14),arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->',color=yellow,lw=1.8)); ax.text(-(R+RI)/2,.22,r'$\Delta r$',color=yellow,fontsize=20,ha='center') ax.plot([0,1.18],[R,R],color=(1,1,1,.45),lw=1,ls='--'); ax.text(1.22,1.02,'OUTER RADIUS',color='white',fontsize=12,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(1.22,.91,f'R = {R:.16f}',color='white',fontsize=11,family='DejaVu Sans Mono') ax.plot([RI,1.18],[0,0],color=cyan,lw=1,ls='--'); ax.text(1.22,.08,'INNER RADIUS',color=cyan,fontsize=12,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(1.22,-.04,r'$r_i = \sqrt{3}/2 \cdot R$',color=cyan,fontsize=11); ax.text(1.22,-.15,f'= {RI:.16f}',color=cyan,fontsize=11,family='DejaVu Sans Mono') ## 1. Purpose

This presentation isolates the first measurable differentiation within the spherical form before the full two-sphere Vesica Piscis configuration is displayed.

The self-relation is defined by $D=R$. The derived internal circle is:

$$
r_i=\sqrt{{R^2-\left(\frac{{D}}{{2}}\right)^2}}=\frac{{\sqrt{{3}}}}{{2}}R
$$

$$

| Relation | Exact | Percentage |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inner | $3/4$ | 75% |
| Differential | $1/4$ | 25% |

REPORT MAP This folder contains the final verification reports for the RP9 system.The reports represent the results of the entire verification chain and serve as the primary audit evidence for the system.Each report documents a specific verification layer and contains the results, checks, and conclusions produced during each run.The folder is intended to be reviewed independently without the reader first needing to study the source code.However, for complete reproducibility, the corresponding source code and module descriptions are available in other parts of the repository.For each verification step, there are three separate representations of the same results.REPORT.md ↓ Readable final report REPORT.json ↓ Original machine output REPORT.json.md ↓ Readable JSON representation The purpose of this division is to separate: human readability original data documented machine output without losing information.The reports should be read in the following order.1. META_VESICA_CORE_FINAL_REPORT ↓ 2. META_EQUILIBRIUM_FINAL_REPORT ↓ 3. META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION_REPORT ↓ 4. FUSION_RESIDUAL_ANALYSIS_REPORT ↓ 5. STEP_ISOLATION_RECONSTRUCTION_REPORT ↓ 6. STEP_ISOLATION_EXTENDED_REPORT ↓ 7. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_LOCK_REPORT ↓ 8. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_LOCK_V2_REPORT ↓ 9. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_PROPAGATION_V3_REPORT ↓ 10. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_PROPAGATION_V4_REPORT ↓ 11. OBSERVER_LOCKED_RELATIONAL_EMERGENCE_V5_REPORT ↓ 12. SELF_ORGANIZING_RELATIONAL_EMERGENCE_V6_REPORT Each report builds on previously verified results.No report replaces a previous report.Each step introduces a new layer of review.Together, the reports describe the entire verification chain:Data generation ↓ Calibration ↓ Sequential derivation ↓ Reproducibility control ↓ Step isolation ↓ Coordinate reconstruction ↓ Coordinate evolution ↓ Coordinate propagation ↓ Observer validation ↓ Self-organizing emergence The reports are therefore intended to be read as a coherent chain rather than as stand-alone documents.Each report contains the verification results produced at each step.The claims in the reports can be reviewed against:REPORT.md ↓ Summary report REPORT.json.md ↓ Readable data display REPORT.json ↓ Original machine output The original JSON file always constitutes the primary reference.The Markdown versions are documentation and presentation layers on top of the same data.The reports are produced by the modules found in the repository's code section.For each report there is:Source code ↓ README ↓ Final report ↓ Original data This enables full traceability from verified results back to the original implementation.This folder constitutes the RP9 system's collective review documentation.The aim is to provide a complete set of verification reports where each result can be reviewed, tracked and compared against its original machine output.Together, the reports represent the complete verification chain from initial data generation to final self-organizing emergence.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.
