item.title: A. FORM. (H-D-R) x3. PYTHON
item.description: import csv import json import subprocess import sys import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.1" try: SCRIPT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve() except NameError: SCRIPT_PATH = Path.cwd() / "(H-D-R)_x4_IN-PTS-Net.py" ROOT_DIR = SCRIPT_PATH.parent FILE_NAME = SCRIPT_PATH.stem # ============================================================ # GLOBAL RENDER FLAGS (IDENTISKT x2) # ============================================================ SHOW_CENTERS = False SHOW_RELATIONS = False SHOW_INTERSECTIONS = False RENDER_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "PNG & HTML" DATA_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "CODE_data_output" RENDER_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def ensure_kaleido(): try: import kaleido return True except Exception: subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido"]) return True def as_float(value): return float(value) def as_list(point): return [float(v) for v in point] def distance_3d(p1, p2): return float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)) def circle_intersections(c1, r1, c2, r2): x1, y1 = c1 x2, y2 = c2 dx = x2 - x1 dy = y2 - y1 d = np.hypot(dx, dy) if d > r1 + r2 or d < abs(r1 - r2) or d == 0: return [] a = (r1**2 - r2**2 + d**2) / (2 * d) h = np.sqrt(r1**2 - a**2) xm = x1 + a * dx / d ym = y1 + a * dy / d rx = -dy * (h / d) ry = dx * (h / d) p1 = np.array([xm + rx, ym + ry]) p2 = np.array([xm - rx, ym - ry]) return [p1, p2] def create_vesica_circles(r, n=200): t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) x1 = r * np.cos(t) - r / 2 y1 = r * np.sin(t) x2 = r * np.cos(t) + r / 2 y2 = r * np.sin(t) return (x1, y1), (x2, y2) def rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az): rad_x = np.deg2rad(ax) rad_y = np.deg2rad(ay) rad_z = np.deg2rad(az) if ax != 0: y, z = ( y * np.cos(rad_x) - z * np.sin(rad_x), y * np.sin(rad_x) + z * np.cos(rad_x) ) if ay != 0: x, z = ( x * np.cos(rad_y) + z * np.sin(rad_y), -x * np.sin(rad_y) + z * np.cos(rad_y) ) if az != 0: x, y = ( x * np.cos(rad_z) - y * np.sin(rad_z), x * np.sin(rad_z) + y * np.cos(rad_z) ) return x, y, z def rotate_point(point, ax, ay, az): x, y, z = point rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az) return np.array([rx, ry, rz]) def vesica_points(r): c1 = np.array([-r / 2, 0]) c2 = np.array([r / 2, 0]) intersections_2d = circle_intersections(c1, r, c2, r) centers = [ np.array([c1[0], c1[1], 0.0]), np.array([c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]) ] intersections = [ np.array([p[0], p[1], 0.0]) for p in intersections_2d ] return centers, intersections # ============================================================ # PARAMETRAR (x4) # ============================================================ r_core = 6.0 r_axis = 3.0 r_diag = 1.5 t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200) COLOR_CORE = "#4da6ff" COLOR_X2 = "#ff4d4d" COLOR_X4 = "#66ff66" LINE_WIDTH = 3 # ============================================================ # LAGER (IDENTISK STRUKTUR + x4) # ============================================================ VESICA_LAYERS = [ {"id": "X1_CORE", "radius": r_core, "color": COLOR_CORE, "rotation": (0, 0, 0)}, {"id": "X2_ROT_X", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (90, 0, 0)}, {"id": "X2_ROT_Y", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (0, 90, 0)}, {"id": "X4_D1", "radius": r_diag, "color": COLOR_X4, "rotation": (45, 45, 0)}, {"id": "X4_D2", "radius": r_diag, "color": COLOR_X4, "rotation": (45, -45, 0)}, {"id": "X4_D3", "radius": r_diag, "color": COLOR_X4, "rotation": (-45, 45, 0)}, {"id": "X4_D4", "radius": r_diag, "color": COLOR_X4, "rotation": (-45, -45, 0)}, ] def add_vesica_to_traces(traces, nodes, labels, r, color, opacity, width, rotation, layer_id): (c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y) = create_vesica_circles(r) for cx, cy in [(c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y)]: z = np.zeros_like(cx) rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(cx, cy, z, *rotation) traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=rx, y=ry, z=rz, mode="lines", line=dict(color=color, width=width), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" )) centers, intersections = vesica_points(r) centers_rot = [rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in centers] inter_rot = [rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in intersections] names = [ layer_id + "_C1", layer_id + "_C2", layer_id + "_I_TOP", layer_id + "_I_BOTTOM" ] for n, p in zip(names, centers_rot + inter_rot): labels.append(n) nodes.append(p) if SHOW_CENTERS: traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in centers_rot], y=[p[1] for p in centers_rot], z=[p[2] for p in centers_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=8, color="gray"), showlegend=False )) if SHOW_INTERSECTIONS: traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in inter_rot], y=[p[1] for p in inter_rot], z=[p[2] for p in inter_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=10, color="white"), showlegend=False )) def build_nodes_and_edges(): nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces([], nodes, labels, layer["radius"], layer["color"], 1.0, LINE_WIDTH, layer["rotation"], layer["id"]) edges = [] for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): edges.append({ "from": labels[i], "to": labels[j], "distance": distance_3d(nodes[i], nodes[j]) }) return nodes, labels, edges all_points, point_labels, edges = build_nodes_and_edges() def build_figure(title_text): traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces(traces, nodes, labels, layer["radius"], layer["color"], 1.0, LINE_WIDTH, layer["rotation"], layer["id"]) if SHOW_RELATIONS: for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] traces.append(go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False )) fig = go.Figure(data=traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": {"camera": dict(eye=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE))}, "V-B": {"camera": dict(eye=dict(x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0))}, "V-C": {"camera": dict(eye=dict(x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0))}, "V-D": {"camera": dict(eye=dict(x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE))} } fig_main = build_figure(FILE_NAME) html_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + ".html") fig_main.write_html(str(html_file)) ensure_kaleido() png_files = [] for view_name, view_data in VIEWS.items(): fig_view = build_figure(FILE_NAME + " - " + view_name) fig_view.update_layout(scene_camera=view_data["camera"]) png_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + view_name + ".png") fig_view.write_image(str(png_file), width=1100, height=650, scale=2) png_files.append(str(png_file)) # ============================================================ # FULL DATA EXPORT (DETTA VAR DET SOM SAKNADES) # ============================================================ data_sheet = { "script": { "file_name": FILE_NAME, "script_path": str(SCRIPT_PATH), "version": SCRIPT_VERSION }, "output": { "render_folder": str(RENDER_DIR), "data_folder": str(DATA_DIR), "html_file": str(html_file), "png_files": png_files }, "parameters": { "radius_core": as_float(r_core), "radius_axis": as_float(r_axis), "radius_diag": as_float(r_diag), "circle_resolution": int(len(t)), "camera_scale": as_float(CAM_SCALE), "color_core": COLOR_CORE, "color_x2": COLOR_X2, "color_x4": COLOR_X4, "line_width": int(LINE_WIDTH) }, "all_points": { point_labels[i]: as_list(all_points[i]) for i in range(len(all_points)) }, "relations_K_n": edges } json_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.json") md_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.md") csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_points.csv") edges_csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_relations.csv") with open(json_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(data_sheet, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False) with open(csv_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow(["point", "x", "y", "z"]) for label, point in zip(point_labels, all_points): writer.writerow([label, *as_list(point)]) with open(edges_csv_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow(["from", "to", "distance"]) for edge in edges: writer.writerow([edge["from"], edge["to"], edge["distance"]]) webbrowser.open("file://" + str(html_file.resolve())) print("") print("EXPORT KLAR") print("HTML:", html_file) print("") for item in png_files: print("PNG:", item) print("") print("DATA:", json_file) print("DATA:", csv_file) print("DATA:", edges_csv_file) ⚖️ — License & CopyrightLicensed under item.description: import csv import json import subprocess import sys import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.1" try: SCRIPT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve() except NameError: SCRIPT_PATH = Path.cwd() / "(H-D-R)_x2_IN-PTS-Net.py" ROOT_DIR = SCRIPT_PATH.parent FILE_NAME = SCRIPT_PATH.stem # ============================================================ # GLOBAL RENDER FLAGS # ============================================================ SHOW_CENTERS = True SHOW_RELATIONS = True SHOW_INTERSECTIONS = True RENDER_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "PNG & HTML" DATA_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "CODE_data_output" RENDER_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def ensure_kaleido(): try: import kaleido return True except Exception: subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido"]) return True def as_float(value): return float(value) def as_list(point): return [float(v) for v in point] def distance_3d(p1, p2): return float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)) def circle_intersections(c1, r1, c2, r2): x1, y1 = c1 x2, y2 = c2 dx = x2 - x1 dy = y2 - y1 d = np.hypot(dx, dy) if d > r1 + r2 or d < abs(r1 - r2) or d == 0: return [] a = (r1**2 - r2**2 + d**2) / (2 * d) h = np.sqrt(r1**2 - a**2) xm = x1 + a * dx / d ym = y1 + a * dy / d rx = -dy * (h / d) ry = dx * (h / d) p1 = np.array([xm + rx, ym + ry]) p2 = np.array([xm - rx, ym - ry]) return [p1, p2] def create_vesica_circles(r, n=200): t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) x1 = r * np.cos(t) - r / 2 y1 = r * np.sin(t) x2 = r * np.cos(t) + r / 2 y2 = r * np.sin(t) return (x1, y1), (x2, y2) def rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az): rad_x = np.deg2rad(ax) rad_y = np.deg2rad(ay) rad_z = np.deg2rad(az) if ax != 0: y, z = ( y * np.cos(rad_x) - z * np.sin(rad_x), y * np.sin(rad_x) + z * np.cos(rad_x) ) if ay != 0: x, z = ( x * np.cos(rad_y) + z * np.sin(rad_y), -x * np.sin(rad_y) + z * np.cos(rad_y) ) if az != 0: x, y = ( x * np.cos(rad_z) - y * np.sin(rad_z), x * np.sin(rad_z) + y * np.cos(rad_z) ) return x, y, z def rotate_point(point, ax, ay, az): x, y, z = point rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az) return np.array([rx, ry, rz]) def vesica_points(r): c1 = np.array([-r / 2, 0]) c2 = np.array([r / 2, 0]) intersections_2d = circle_intersections(c1, r, c2, r) centers = [ np.array([c1[0], c1[1], 0.0]), np.array([c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]) ] intersections = [ np.array([p[0], p[1], 0.0]) for p in intersections_2d ] return centers, intersections r_core = 6.0 r_axis = 3.0 t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200) COLOR_CORE = "#4da6ff" COLOR_X2 = "#ff4d4d" LINE_WIDTH = 3 VESICA_LAYERS = [ { "id": "X1_CORE", "radius": r_core, "color": COLOR_CORE, "rotation": (0, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_X", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (90, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_Y", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (0, 90, 0) } ] def add_vesica_to_traces(traces, nodes, labels, r, color, opacity, width, rotation, layer_id): (c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y) = create_vesica_circles(r) for cx, cy in [(c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y)]: z = np.zeros_like(cx) rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(cx, cy, z, *rotation) traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=rx, y=ry, z=rz, mode="lines", line=dict(color=color, width=width), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) centers, intersections = vesica_points(r) centers_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in centers ] intersections_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in intersections ] points = centers_rot + intersections_rot point_names = [ layer_id + "_C1", layer_id + "_C2", layer_id + "_I_TOP", layer_id + "_I_BOTTOM" ] for point_name, point in zip(point_names, points): labels.append(point_name) nodes.append(point) if SHOW_CENTERS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in centers_rot], y=[p[1] for p in centers_rot], z=[p[2] for p in centers_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=8, color="gray"), name=layer_id + "_CENTERS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) if SHOW_INTERSECTIONS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in intersections_rot], y=[p[1] for p in intersections_rot], z=[p[2] for p in intersections_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=10, color="white"), name=layer_id + "_INTERSECTIONS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) def build_nodes_and_edges(): nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: layer_nodes = [] layer_labels = [] add_vesica_to_traces( [], layer_nodes, layer_labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) nodes.extend(layer_nodes) labels.extend(layer_labels) edges = [] for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): edges.append({ "from": labels[i], "to": labels[j], "distance": distance_3d(nodes[i], nodes[j]) }) return nodes, labels, edges all_points, point_labels, edges = build_nodes_and_edges() def build_figure(title_text): all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) if SHOW_RELATIONS: for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": { "description": "Topvy: full Vesica-form synlig.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=1.0, z=0.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-B": { "description": "Sidovy X: intersektionerna blir ytterpunkter, centrum kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-C": { "description": "Sidovy Y: centrum blir ytterpunkter, intersektionerna kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-D": { "description": "Diagonal/iso-vy: full relation synlig i sned projektion.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) } } fig_main = build_figure(FILE_NAME) html_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + ".html") fig_main.write_html(str(html_file)) ensure_kaleido() png_files = [] for view_name, view_data in VIEWS.items(): fig_view = build_figure(FILE_NAME + " - " + view_name) fig_view.update_layout(scene_camera=view_data["camera"]) png_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + view_name + ".png") fig_view.write_image(str(png_file), width=1100, height=650, scale=2) png_files.append(str(png_file)) data_sheet = { "script": { "file_name": FILE_NAME, "script_path": str(SCRIPT_PATH), "version": SCRIPT_VERSION }, "output": { "render_folder": str(RENDER_DIR), "data_folder": str(DATA_DIR), "html_file": str(html_file), "png_files": png_files }, "parameters": { "radius_core": as_float(r_core), "radius_axis": as_float(r_axis), "circle_resolution": int(len(t)), "camera_scale": as_float(CAM_SCALE), "color_core": COLOR_CORE, "color_x2": COLOR_X2, "line_width": int(LINE_WIDTH), "layers": [ { "id": layer["id"], "radius": as_float(layer["radius"]), "color": layer["color"], "rotation": list(layer["rotation"]) } for layer in VESICA_LAYERS ] }, "all_points": { point_labels[i]: as_list(all_points[i]) for i in range(len(all_points)) }, "relations_K_n": edges, "views": { key: { "description": value["description"], "camera": value["camera"] } for key, value in VIEWS.items() } } json_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.json") md_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.md") csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_points.csv") edges_csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_relations.csv") with open(json_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(data_sheet, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False) md_lines = [] md_lines.append("# " + FILE_NAME + " datasheet") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Script") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- File name: `" + FILE_NAME + "`") md_lines.append("- Version: `" + SCRIPT_VERSION + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Output") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- HTML: `" + str(html_file) + "`") md_lines.append("- Render folder: `" + str(RENDER_DIR) + "`") md_lines.append("- Data folder: `" + str(DATA_DIR) + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Parameters") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- Radius core: `" + str(as_float(r_core)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Radius axis: `" + str(as_float(r_axis)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Circle resolution: `" + str(len(t)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Camera scale: `" + str(as_float(CAM_SCALE)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Color core: `" + COLOR_CORE + "`") md_lines.append("- Color x2: `" + COLOR_X2 + "`") md_lines.append("- Line width: `" + str(LINE_WIDTH) + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Layers") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| Layer | Radius | Color | Rotation |") md_lines.append("|---|---:|---|---|") for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: md_lines.append( "| " + layer["id"] + " | " + str(as_float(layer["radius"])) + " | " + layer["color"] + " | " + str(list(layer["rotation"])) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Points") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| Point | X | Y | Z |") md_lines.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|") for label, point in zip(point_labels, all_points): md_lines.append( "| " + label + " | " + str(as_float(point[0])) + " | " + str(as_float(point[1])) + " | " + str(as_float(point[2])) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Relations") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| From | To | Distance |") md_lines.append("|---|---|---:|") for edge in edges: md_lines.append( "| " + edge["from"] + " | " + edge["to"] + " | " + str(edge["distance"]) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Views") md_lines.append("") for key, value in VIEWS.items(): md_lines.append("### " + key) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append(value["description"]) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- PNG: `" + str(RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + key + ".png")) + "`") md_lines.append("- Camera: `" + json.dumps(value["camera"], ensure_ascii=False) + "`") md_lines.append("") with open(md_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n".join(md_lines)) with open(csv_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow(["point", "x", "y", "z"]) for label, point in zip(point_labels, all_points): writer.writerow([label, as_float(point[0]), as_float(point[1]), as_float(point[2])]) with open(edges_csv_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow(["from", "to", "distance"]) for edge in edges: writer.writerow([edge["from"], edge["to"], edge["distance"]]) webbrowser.open("file://" + str(html_file.resolve())) print("") print("EXPORT KLAR") print("HTML:", html_file) print("") for item in png_files: print("PNG:", item) print("") print("DATA:", json_file) print("DATA:", md_file) print("DATA:", csv_file) print("DATA:", edges_csv_file) ⚖️ — License & CopyrightLicensed under item.title: B. NODES. (H-D-R) x2. PYTHON
item.description: import csv import json import subprocess import sys import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.1" try: SCRIPT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve() except NameError: SCRIPT_PATH = Path.cwd() / "(H-D-R)_x2_IN-PTS-Net.py" ROOT_DIR = SCRIPT_PATH.parent FILE_NAME = SCRIPT_PATH.stem # ============================================================ # GLOBAL RENDER FLAGS # ============================================================ SHOW_CENTERS = True SHOW_RELATIONS = False SHOW_INTERSECTIONS = False RENDER_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "PNG & HTML" DATA_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "CODE_data_output" RENDER_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def ensure_kaleido(): try: import kaleido return True except Exception: subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido"]) return True def as_float(value): return float(value) def as_list(point): return [float(v) for v in point] def distance_3d(p1, p2): return float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)) def circle_intersections(c1, r1, c2, r2): x1, y1 = c1 x2, y2 = c2 dx = x2 - x1 dy = y2 - y1 d = np.hypot(dx, dy) if d > r1 + r2 or d < abs(r1 - r2) or d == 0: return [] a = (r1**2 - r2**2 + d**2) / (2 * d) h = np.sqrt(r1**2 - a**2) xm = x1 + a * dx / d ym = y1 + a * dy / d rx = -dy * (h / d) ry = dx * (h / d) p1 = np.array([xm + rx, ym + ry]) p2 = np.array([xm - rx, ym - ry]) return [p1, p2] def create_vesica_circles(r, n=200): t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) x1 = r * np.cos(t) - r / 2 y1 = r * np.sin(t) x2 = r * np.cos(t) + r / 2 y2 = r * np.sin(t) return (x1, y1), (x2, y2) def rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az): rad_x = np.deg2rad(ax) rad_y = np.deg2rad(ay) rad_z = np.deg2rad(az) if ax != 0: y, z = ( y * np.cos(rad_x) - z * np.sin(rad_x), y * np.sin(rad_x) + z * np.cos(rad_x) ) if ay != 0: x, z = ( x * np.cos(rad_y) + z * np.sin(rad_y), -x * np.sin(rad_y) + z * np.cos(rad_y) ) if az != 0: x, y = ( x * np.cos(rad_z) - y * np.sin(rad_z), x * np.sin(rad_z) + y * np.cos(rad_z) ) return x, y, z def rotate_point(point, ax, ay, az): x, y, z = point rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az) return np.array([rx, ry, rz]) def vesica_points(r): c1 = np.array([-r / 2, 0]) c2 = np.array([r / 2, 0]) intersections_2d = circle_intersections(c1, r, c2, r) centers = [ np.array([c1[0], c1[1], 0.0]), np.array([c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]) ] intersections = [ np.array([p[0], p[1], 0.0]) for p in intersections_2d ] return centers, intersections r_core = 6.0 r_axis = 3.0 t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200) COLOR_CORE = "#4da6ff" COLOR_X2 = "#ff4d4d" LINE_WIDTH = 3 VESICA_LAYERS = [ { "id": "X1_CORE", "radius": r_core, "color": COLOR_CORE, "rotation": (0, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_X", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (90, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_Y", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (0, 90, 0) } ] def add_vesica_to_traces(traces, nodes, labels, r, color, opacity, width, rotation, layer_id): (c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y) = create_vesica_circles(r) for cx, cy in [(c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y)]: z = np.zeros_like(cx) rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(cx, cy, z, *rotation) traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=rx, y=ry, z=rz, mode="lines", line=dict(color=color, width=width), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) centers, intersections = vesica_points(r) centers_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in centers ] intersections_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in intersections ] points = centers_rot + intersections_rot point_names = [ layer_id + "_C1", layer_id + "_C2", layer_id + "_I_TOP", layer_id + "_I_BOTTOM" ] for point_name, point in zip(point_names, points): labels.append(point_name) nodes.append(point) if SHOW_CENTERS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in centers_rot], y=[p[1] for p in centers_rot], z=[p[2] for p in centers_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=8, color="gray"), name=layer_id + "_CENTERS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) if SHOW_INTERSECTIONS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in intersections_rot], y=[p[1] for p in intersections_rot], z=[p[2] for p in intersections_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=10, color="white"), name=layer_id + "_INTERSECTIONS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) def build_nodes_and_edges(): nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: layer_nodes = [] layer_labels = [] add_vesica_to_traces( [], layer_nodes, layer_labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) nodes.extend(layer_nodes) labels.extend(layer_labels) edges = [] for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): edges.append({ "from": labels[i], "to": labels[j], "distance": distance_3d(nodes[i], nodes[j]) }) return nodes, labels, edges all_points, point_labels, edges = build_nodes_and_edges() def build_figure(title_text): all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) if SHOW_RELATIONS: for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": { "description": "Topvy: full Vesica-form synlig.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=1.0, z=0.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-B": { "description": "Sidovy X: intersektionerna blir ytterpunkter, centrum kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-C": { "description": "Sidovy Y: centrum blir ytterpunkter, intersektionerna kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-D": { "description": "Diagonal/iso-vy: full relation synlig i sned projektion.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) } } fig_main = build_figure(FILE_NAME) html_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + ".html") fig_main.write_html(str(html_file)) ensure_kaleido() png_files = [] for view_name, view_data in VIEWS.items(): fig_view = build_figure(FILE_NAME + " - " + view_name) fig_view.update_layout(scene_camera=view_data["camera"]) png_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + view_name + ".png") fig_view.write_image(str(png_file), width=1100, height=650, scale=2) png_files.append(str(png_file)) data_sheet = { "script": { "file_name": FILE_NAME, "script_path": str(SCRIPT_PATH), "version": SCRIPT_VERSION }, "output": { "render_folder": str(RENDER_DIR), "data_folder": str(DATA_DIR), "html_file": str(html_file), "png_files": png_files }, "parameters": { "radius_core": as_float(r_core), "radius_axis": as_float(r_axis), "circle_resolution": int(len(t)), "camera_scale": as_float(CAM_SCALE), "color_core": COLOR_CORE, "color_x2": COLOR_X2, "line_width": int(LINE_WIDTH), "layers": [ { "id": layer["id"], "radius": as_float(layer["radius"]), "color": layer["color"], "rotation": list(layer["rotation"]) } for layer in VESICA_LAYERS ] }, "all_points": { point_labels[i]: as_list(all_points[i]) for i in range(len(all_points)) }, "relations_K_n": edges, "views": { key: { "description": value["description"], "camera": value["camera"] } for key, value in VIEWS.items() } } json_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.json") md_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_datasheet.md") csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_points.csv") edges_csv_file = DATA_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "_relations.csv") with open(json_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(data_sheet, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False) md_lines = [] md_lines.append("# " + FILE_NAME + " datasheet") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Script") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- File name: `" + FILE_NAME + "`") md_lines.append("- Version: `" + SCRIPT_VERSION + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Output") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- HTML: `" + str(html_file) + "`") md_lines.append("- Render folder: `" + str(RENDER_DIR) + "`") md_lines.append("- Data folder: `" + str(DATA_DIR) + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Parameters") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- Radius core: `" + str(as_float(r_core)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Radius axis: `" + str(as_float(r_axis)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Circle resolution: `" + str(len(t)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Camera scale: `" + str(as_float(CAM_SCALE)) + "`") md_lines.append("- Color core: `" + COLOR_CORE + "`") md_lines.append("- Color x2: `" + COLOR_X2 + "`") md_lines.append("- Line width: `" + str(LINE_WIDTH) + "`") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Layers") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| Layer | Radius | Color | Rotation |") md_lines.append("|---|---:|---|---|") for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: md_lines.append( "| " + layer["id"] + " | " + str(as_float(layer["radius"])) + " | " + layer["color"] + " | " + str(list(layer["rotation"])) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Points") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| Point | X | Y | Z |") md_lines.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|") for label, point in zip(point_labels, all_points): md_lines.append( "| " + label + " | " + str(as_float(point[0])) + " | " + str(as_float(point[1])) + " | " + str(as_float(point[2])) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Relations") md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("| From | To | Distance |") md_lines.append("|---|---|---:|") for edge in edges: md_lines.append( "| " + edge["from"] + " | " + edge["to"] + " | " + str(edge["distance"]) + " |" ) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("## Views") md_lines.append("") for key, value in VIEWS.items(): md_lines.append("### " + key) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append(value["description"]) md_lines.append("") md_lines.append("- PNG: `" + str(RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + key + ".png")) + "`") md_lines.append("- Camera: `" + json.dumps(value["camera"], ensure_ascii=False) + "`") md_lines.append("") with open(md_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n".join(md_lines)) with open(csv_file, "w", newline="", item.title: A. FORM. (H-D-R) x2. PYTHON
item.description: import csv import json import subprocess import sys import webbrowser from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.1" try: SCRIPT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve() except NameError: SCRIPT_PATH = Path.cwd() / "(H-D-R)_x2_IN-PTS-Net.py" ROOT_DIR = SCRIPT_PATH.parent FILE_NAME = SCRIPT_PATH.stem # ============================================================ # GLOBAL RENDER FLAGS # ============================================================ SHOW_CENTERS = False SHOW_RELATIONS = False SHOW_INTERSECTIONS = False RENDER_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "PNG & HTML" DATA_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "CODE_data_output" RENDER_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def ensure_kaleido(): try: import kaleido return True except Exception: subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido"]) return True def as_float(value): return float(value) def as_list(point): return [float(v) for v in point] def distance_3d(p1, p2): return float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)) def circle_intersections(c1, r1, c2, r2): x1, y1 = c1 x2, y2 = c2 dx = x2 - x1 dy = y2 - y1 d = np.hypot(dx, dy) if d > r1 + r2 or d < abs(r1 - r2) or d == 0: return [] a = (r1**2 - r2**2 + d**2) / (2 * d) h = np.sqrt(r1**2 - a**2) xm = x1 + a * dx / d ym = y1 + a * dy / d rx = -dy * (h / d) ry = dx * (h / d) p1 = np.array([xm + rx, ym + ry]) p2 = np.array([xm - rx, ym - ry]) return [p1, p2] def create_vesica_circles(r, n=200): t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) x1 = r * np.cos(t) - r / 2 y1 = r * np.sin(t) x2 = r * np.cos(t) + r / 2 y2 = r * np.sin(t) return (x1, y1), (x2, y2) def rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az): rad_x = np.deg2rad(ax) rad_y = np.deg2rad(ay) rad_z = np.deg2rad(az) if ax != 0: y, z = ( y * np.cos(rad_x) - z * np.sin(rad_x), y * np.sin(rad_x) + z * np.cos(rad_x) ) if ay != 0: x, z = ( x * np.cos(rad_y) + z * np.sin(rad_y), -x * np.sin(rad_y) + z * np.cos(rad_y) ) if az != 0: x, y = ( x * np.cos(rad_z) - y * np.sin(rad_z), x * np.sin(rad_z) + y * np.cos(rad_z) ) return x, y, z def rotate_point(point, ax, ay, az): x, y, z = point rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(x, y, z, ax, ay, az) return np.array([rx, ry, rz]) def vesica_points(r): c1 = np.array([-r / 2, 0]) c2 = np.array([r / 2, 0]) intersections_2d = circle_intersections(c1, r, c2, r) centers = [ np.array([c1[0], c1[1], 0.0]), np.array([c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]) ] intersections = [ np.array([p[0], p[1], 0.0]) for p in intersections_2d ] return centers, intersections r_core = 6.0 r_axis = 3.0 t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200) COLOR_CORE = "#4da6ff" COLOR_X2 = "#ff4d4d" LINE_WIDTH = 3 VESICA_LAYERS = [ { "id": "X1_CORE", "radius": r_core, "color": COLOR_CORE, "rotation": (0, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_X", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (90, 0, 0) }, { "id": "X2_ROT_Y", "radius": r_axis, "color": COLOR_X2, "rotation": (0, 90, 0) } ] def add_vesica_to_traces(traces, nodes, labels, r, color, opacity, width, rotation, layer_id): (c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y) = create_vesica_circles(r) for cx, cy in [(c1_x, c1_y), (c2_x, c2_y)]: z = np.zeros_like(cx) rx, ry, rz = rotate_3d(cx, cy, z, *rotation) traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=rx, y=ry, z=rz, mode="lines", line=dict(color=color, width=width), opacity=opacity, showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) centers, intersections = vesica_points(r) centers_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in centers ] intersections_rot = [ rotate_point(p, *rotation) for p in intersections ] points = centers_rot + intersections_rot point_names = [ layer_id + "_C1", layer_id + "_C2", layer_id + "_I_TOP", layer_id + "_I_BOTTOM" ] for point_name, point in zip(point_names, points): labels.append(point_name) nodes.append(point) if SHOW_CENTERS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in centers_rot], y=[p[1] for p in centers_rot], z=[p[2] for p in centers_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=8, color="gray"), name=layer_id + "_CENTERS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) if SHOW_INTERSECTIONS: traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in intersections_rot], y=[p[1] for p in intersections_rot], z=[p[2] for p in intersections_rot], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=10, color="white"), name=layer_id + "_INTERSECTIONS", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) def build_nodes_and_edges(): nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: layer_nodes = [] layer_labels = [] add_vesica_to_traces( [], layer_nodes, layer_labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) nodes.extend(layer_nodes) labels.extend(layer_labels) edges = [] for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): edges.append({ "from": labels[i], "to": labels[j], "distance": distance_3d(nodes[i], nodes[j]) }) return nodes, labels, edges all_points, point_labels, edges = build_nodes_and_edges() def build_figure(title_text): all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) if SHOW_RELATIONS: for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig all_traces = [] nodes = [] labels = [] for layer in VESICA_LAYERS: add_vesica_to_traces( all_traces, nodes, labels, r=layer["radius"], color=layer["color"], opacity=1.0, width=LINE_WIDTH, rotation=layer["rotation"], layer_id=layer["id"] ) for i in range(len(nodes)): for j in range(i + 1, len(nodes)): p1 = nodes[i] p2 = nodes[j] all_traces.append( go.Scatter3d( x=[p1[0], p2[0]], y=[p1[1], p2[1]], z=[p1[2], p2[2]], mode="lines", line=dict(width=1, color="white"), showlegend=False, hoverinfo="none" ) ) fig = go.Figure(data=all_traces) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": { "description": "Topvy: full Vesica-form synlig.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=1.0, z=0.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-B": { "description": "Sidovy X: intersektionerna blir ytterpunkter, centrum kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-C": { "description": "Sidovy Y: centrum blir ytterpunkter, intersektionerna kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-D": { "description": "Diagonal/iso-vy: full relation synlig i sned projektion.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) } } fig_main = build_figure(FILE_NAME) html_file = Installerar kaleido...") subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "kaleido"]) return True # ============================================================ # HJALPFUNKTIONER # ============================================================ def as_float(value): return float(value) def as_list(point): return [float(v) for v in point] def distance_3d(p1, p2): return float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)) # ============================================================ # EXAKT CIRKEL-CIRKEL INTERSEKTION # ============================================================ def circle_intersections(c1, r1, c2, r2): x1, y1 = c1 x2, y2 = c2 dx = x2 - x1 dy = y2 - y1 d = np.hypot(dx, dy) if d > r1 + r2 or d < abs(r1 - r2) or d == 0: return [] a = (r1**2 - r2**2 + d**2) / (2 * d) h = np.sqrt(r1**2 - a**2) xm = x1 + a * dx / d ym = y1 + a * dy / d rx = -dy * (h / d) ry = dx * (h / d) p1 = np.array([xm + rx, ym + ry]) p2 = np.array([xm - rx, ym - ry]) return [p1, p2] # ============================================================ # VESICA DATA # ============================================================ r = 6.0 c1 = np.array([-r / 2, 0]) c2 = np.array([r / 2, 0]) intersections_2d = circle_intersections(c1, r, c2, r) intersections = [ np.array([p[0], p[1], 0.0]) for p in intersections_2d ] centers = [ np.array([c1[0], c1[1], 0.0]), np.array([c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]) ] all_points = centers + intersections point_labels = [ "C1", "C2", "I_TOP", "I_BOTTOM" ] edges = [] for i in range(len(all_points)): for j in range(i + 1, len(all_points)): edges.append({ "from": point_labels[i], "to": point_labels[j], "distance": distance_3d(all_points[i], all_points[j]) }) # ============================================================ # CIRKLAR # ============================================================ t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200) x1 = r * np.cos(t) - r / 2 y1 = r * np.sin(t) z1 = np.zeros_like(x1) x2 = r * np.cos(t) + r / 2 y2 = r * np.sin(t) z2 = np.zeros_like(x2) # ============================================================ # FIGUR BYGG # ============================================================ def build_figure(title_text): fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=x1, y=y1, z=z1, mode="lines", line=dict(color="blue"), name="trace 0" )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=x2, y=y2, z=z2, mode="lines", line=dict(color="blue"), name="trace 1" )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in centers], y=[p[1] for p in centers], z=[p[2] for p in centers], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=8, color="gray"), name="Centrum" )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=[p[0] for p in intersections], y=[p[1] for p in intersections], z=[p[2] for p in intersections], mode="markers", marker=dict(size=10, color="white"), name="Intersektion" )) fig.update_layout( title=title_text, template="plotly_dark", width=1100, height=650, paper_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", plot_bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)", margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=60, b=0), scene=dict( aspectmode="data", xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False), zaxis=dict(visible=False), bgcolor="rgb(17,17,17)" ) ) return fig # ============================================================ # VYER - NAMN LAASTA MOT RATT VINKEL # ============================================================ CAM_SCALE = 1.5 VIEWS = { "V-A": { "description": "Topvy: full Vesica-form synlig.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=1.0, z=0.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-B": { "description": "Sidovy X: intersektionerna blir ytterpunkter, centrum kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, y=0.0, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-C": { "description": "Sidovy Y: centrum blir ytterpunkter, intersektionerna kollapsar mot mitten.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=0.0, y=2.0 * CAM_SCALE, z=0.0), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) }, "V-D": { "description": "Diagonal/iso-vy: full relation synlig i sned projektion.", "camera": dict( eye=dict(x=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, y=1.5 * CAM_SCALE, z=1.0 * CAM_SCALE), up=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0), center=dict(x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0) ) } } # ============================================================ # HTML EXPORT - ENDAST EN INTERAKTIV HTML # ============================================================ fig_main = build_figure(FILE_NAME) html_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + ".html") fig_main.write_html(str(html_file)) # view_name, view_data in VIEWS.items(): fig_view = build_figure(FILE_NAME + " - " + view_name) fig_view.update_layout(scene_camera=view_data["camera"]) png_file = RENDER_DIR / (FILE_NAME + "__" + stability conditions.The purpose is to investigate whether the coordinate structure can maintain stability, reproducibility, and continuity even under internal reorganization and dynamic change.This connections, and internal structure.Examines how the coordinate field changes under loading, expansion, and internal reorganization.The purpose is to identify whether the structure remains stable under change.Analyzes how internal connections can be reshaped without losing the basic structure of the system.The focus is on: stability continuity reproducibility structural coherence Examines how the coordinate structure evolves through multiple levels and scales.The purpose is to verify that previously established relations remain consistent during continued development.Recreates and establishes the coordinates that arise from the self-organizing process.These are used as a basis for the final verification.Examines how the coordinate structure is affected by changing observation conditions.The purpose is to investigate whether the stability of the system persists even when observation patterns change.Compares the results with previous generations and verifies that the item.title: C. (M-S-D). PYTHON
item.description:
C. (M-S-D) # ============================================================ # META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION.py # Version: 1.0.0 # Purpose: Sequential relational derivation kernel. # Standard: Final permanent derivation layer for RP9. # ============================================================ import csv import json import math import os import sys from datetime import datetime from pathlib import Path try: import numpy as np except Exception as exc: print('ERROR: numpy is required. Install with: pip install numpy') print(str(exc)) sys.exit(2) VERSION = '1.0.0' SCRIPT_NAME = Path(__file__).name ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent CORE_OUTPUT_NAME = 'META_VESICA_CORE_OUTPUT' PIPELINE_OUTPUT_NAME = 'META_EQUILIBRIUM_FINAL' SEQUENTIAL_OUTPUT_NAME = 'META_SEQUENTIAL_OUTPUT' EPS = 1.0e-9 MACHINE_TOL = 1.0e-12 VIEW_GROUPS = { 'A': { 'views': { 'A1': (1.0, 0.0, 0.0), 'A2': (-1.0, 0.0, 0.0), 'A3': (0.0, 1.0, 0.0), 'A4': (0.0, -1.0, 0.0), 'A5': (0.0, 0.0, 1.0), 'A6': (0.0, 0.0, -1.0), } }, 'B': { 'views': { 'B1': (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), 'B2': (1.0, -1.0, 0.0), 'B3': (-1.0, 1.0, 0.0), 'B4': (-1.0, -1.0, 0.0), 'B5': (1.0, 0.0, 1.0), 'B6': (-1.0, 0.0, -1.0), } }, 'C': { 'views': { 'C1': (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), 'C2': (1.0, 1.0, -1.0), 'C3': (1.0, -1.0, 1.0), 'C4': (1.0, -1.0, -1.0), 'C5': (-1.0, 1.0, 1.0), 'C6': (-1.0, 1.0, -1.0), 'C7': (-1.0, -1.0, 1.0), 'C8': (-1.0, -1.0, -1.0), } }, } PAIR_PLAN = [ ['A1-A2', 'A1', 'A2'], ['A3-A4', 'A3', 'A4'], ['A5-A6', 'A5', 'A6'], ['B1-B4', 'B1', 'B4'], ['B2-B3', 'B2', 'B3'], ['B5-B6', 'B5', 'B6'], ['C1-C8', 'C1', 'C8'], ['C2-C7', 'C2', 'C7'], ['C3-C6', 'C3', 'C6'], ['C4-C5', 'C4', 'C5'], ] # ============================================================ # BASIC IO # ============================================================ def now_stamp(): return datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') def iso_stamp(): return datetime.now().isoformat() def write_json(path, data): Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with Path(path).open('w', encoding='utf-8') as f: json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) def write_text(path, text): Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with Path(path).open('w', encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(text) def write_csv(path, rows, fieldnames): Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with Path(path).open('w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f: writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames) writer.writeheader() for row in rows: writer.writerow(row) # ============================================================ # PATH RESOLUTION # ============================================================ def find_directory(name): direct = ROOT_DIR / name if direct.exists() and direct.is_dir(): return direct matches = [] for path in ROOT_DIR.rglob(name): if path.is_dir(): matches.append(path) if matches: matches.sort(key=lambda p: (len(str(p)), str(p))) return matches[0] raise FileNotFoundError('Missing directory: ' + str(name)) CORE_ROOT = find_directory(CORE_OUTPUT_NAME) PIPELINE_ROOT = find_directory(PIPELINE_OUTPUT_NAME) OUTPUT_ROOT = ROOT_DIR / SEQUENTIAL_OUTPUT_NAME LOG_PATH = OUTPUT_ROOT / 'META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION.log' SECTIONS = { 'core': OUTPUT_ROOT / '01_Core_Derivation', 'pairs': OUTPUT_ROOT / '02_Pair_Derivation', 'projection': OUTPUT_ROOT / '03_Projection_Compression', 'symbolic': OUTPUT_ROOT / '04_Symbolic_Lock', 'residual': OUTPUT_ROOT / '05_Residual_Sequence', 'meta': OUTPUT_ROOT / '06_Meta_Equilibrium_Derivation', 'final': OUTPUT_ROOT / '07_Final_Sequential_Report', } for section in SECTIONS.values(): section.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) # ============================================================ # LOGGING # ============================================================ def log_line(message): line = '[' + now_stamp() + '] ' + str(message) print(line) with LOG_PATH.open('a', encoding='utf-8') as f: f.write(line + '
') # ============================================================ # VECTOR CORE # ============================================================ def vec_sub(a, b): return [a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]] def vec_add(a, b): return [a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1], a[2] + b[2]] def vec_mul(a, scalar): return [a[0] * scalar, a[1] * scalar, a[2] * scalar] def vec_norm(a): return math.sqrt((a[0] * a[0]) + (a[1] * a[1]) + (a[2] * a[2])) def vec_close(a, b, eps=EPS): return vec_norm(vec_sub(a, b)) <= eps def midpoint(a, b): return [ (a[0] + b[0]) / 2.0, (a[1] + b[1]) / 2.0, (a[2] + b[2]) / 2.0, ] def normalize(v): n = vec_norm(v) if n <= EPS: return [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] return [v[0] / n, v[1] / n, v[2] / n] # ============================================================ # RELATION CHECKS # ============================================================ def is_opposite(v1, v2): return vec_close(v1, vec_mul(v2, -1.0)) def same_plane(v1, v2): return abs(v1[1]) <= EPS and abs(v2[1]) <= EPS def center_invariant(v1, v2): return vec_close(midpoint(v1, v2), [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]) def delta_nonzero(v): return vec_norm(v) > EPS def active_axes(v): axes = [] if abs(v[0]) > EPS: axes.append('X') if abs(v[1]) > EPS: axes.append('Y') if abs(v[2]) > EPS: axes.append('Z') return axes def three_line_lock(v): return active_axes(v) == ['X', 'Z'] # ============================================================ # PAIR ANALYSIS # ============================================================ def view_vector(name): for group in VIEW_GROUPS.values(): if name in group['views']: return list(group['views'][name]) raise ValueError('Unknown view: ' + str(name)) def verify_pair(pair_name, v1, v2): result = { 'pair': pair_name, 'v1': v1, 'v2': v2, 'is_opposite': bool(is_opposite(v1, v2)), 'same_plane': bool(same_plane(v1, v2)), 'center_invariant': bool(center_invariant(v1, v2)), 'delta_nonzero': bool(delta_nonzero(v1)), 'three_line_lock': bool(three_line_lock(v1)), 'axes': active_axes(v1), 'Z_PASS': False, } result['Z_PASS'] = bool( result['is_opposite'] and result['same_plane'] and result['center_invariant'] and result['delta_nonzero'] and result['three_line_lock'] ) return result # ============================================================ # PROJECTION COMPRESSION # ============================================================ def analysis_projection_basis(direction): vec = np.array(direction, dtype=float) norm = np.linalg.norm(vec) if norm <= 1.0e-12: vec = np.array([1.0, 1.0, 1.0]) else: vec = vec / norm ref = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]) if abs(np.dot(ref, vec)) > 0.98: ref = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]) u = np.cross(ref, vec) u = u / np.linalg.norm(u) v = np.cross(vec, u) v = v / np.linalg.norm(v) return u, v, vec def project_points(points, direction): u, v, _ = analysis_projection_basis(direction) projected = [] for point in points: px = float(np.dot(point, u)) py = float(np.dot(point, v)) projected.append([px, py]) return projected # ============================================================ # CORE DATA IMPORT # ============================================================ def read_json(path): with Path(path).open('r', encoding='utf-8') as f: return json.load(f) SUMMARY_PATH = CORE_ROOT / 'System_Renders_ABC_100' / '00_Metadata' / 'SUMMARY.json' TRACE_PATH = CORE_ROOT / '02_Residual_Trace' / 'STEP_ISOLATION_NUMERIC_RESIDUAL_TRACE.json' FINAL_LOCK_PATH = PIPELINE_ROOT / '04_Meta_Equilibrium' / 'META_EQUILIBRIUM_STATE_LOCK.json' SUMMARY = read_json(SUMMARY_PATH) TRACE = read_json(TRACE_PATH) FINAL_LOCK = read_json(FINAL_LOCK_PATH) # ============================================================ # SEQUENTIAL DERIVATION # ============================================================ def build_pair_derivation(): rows = [] for pair_name, left, right in PAIR_PLAN: v1 = view_vector(left) v2 = view_vector(right) result = verify_pair(pair_name, v1, v2) rows.append(result) write_json(SECTIONS['pairs'] / 'PAIR_DERIVATION.json', rows) write_csv( SECTIONS['pairs'] / 'PAIR_DERIVATION.csv', rows, list(rows[0].keys()) ) return rows # ============================================================ # SYMBOLIC DERIVATION # ============================================================ def build_symbolic_derivation(): delta = math.sqrt(3.0) - 1.0 sigma_delta = delta + (-delta) payload = { 'generated': iso_stamp(), 'symbolic_chain': { 'Delta_nonzero': abs(delta) > MACHINE_TOL, 'Sigma_Delta_zero': abs(sigma_delta) <= MACHINE_TOL, 'B5_equals_negative_B6': True, 'center_invariant': True, 'projection_compression': '3D -> 2D', 'relation_first': True, }, 'final_lock_pass': FINAL_LOCK['final_pass'], } write_json(SECTIONS['symbolic'] / 'SYMBOLIC_DERIVATION.json', payload) return payload # ============================================================ # RESIDUAL DERIVATION # ============================================================ def build_residual_derivation(): lock = TRACE.get('machine_precision_lock', {}) payload = { 'generated': iso_stamp(), 'R16': lock.get('R16'), 'R15': lock.get('R15'), 'ratio': lock.get('R15_div_R16'), 'machine_precision': True, } write_json(SECTIONS['residual'] / 'RESIDUAL_SEQUENCE.json', payload) return payload # ============================================================ # META EQUILIBRIUM DERIVATION # ============================================================ def build_meta_derivation(pair_rows): b5b6 = None for row in pair_rows: if row['pair'] == 'B5-B6': b5b6 = row break payload = { 'generated': iso_stamp(), 'derivation_chain': [ 'Potential', 'Relation', 'Projection', 'Compression', 'Residual Lock', 'B5-B6 Selection', 'META-EQUILIBRIUM', ], 'B5_B6': b5b6, 'META_EQUILIBRIUM_LOCKED': FINAL_LOCK['final_pass'], } write_json(SECTIONS['meta'] / 'META_EQUILIBRIUM_DERIVATION.json', payload) return payload # ============================================================ # FINAL REPORT # ============================================================ def build_final_report(pair_rows, symbolic, residual, meta): total_pairs = len(pair_rows) z_pass_pairs = len([r for r in pair_rows if r['Z_PASS']]) lines = [] lines.append('# META SEQUENTIAL DERIVATION REPORT') lines.append('') lines.append('## FINAL STATUS') lines.append('') lines.append('```text') lines.append('SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION_LOCKED = True') lines.append('```') lines.append('') lines.append('## STRUCTURAL CHAIN') lines.append('') lines.append('```text') lines.append('META_VESICA_CORE.py') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('META_EQUILIBRIUM_PIPELINE.py') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION.py') lines.append('```') lines.append('') lines.append('## PAIR RESULTS') lines.append('') lines.append('| Pair | Z_PASS |') lines.append('|---|---:|') for row in pair_rows: lines.append('| ' + row['pair'] + ' | ' + str(row['Z_PASS']) + ' |') lines.append('') lines.append('## CORE OBSERVATION') lines.append('') lines.append('```text') lines.append('Only B5-B6 preserves:') lines.append('- opposite relation') lines.append('- XZ plane relation') lines.append('- center invariance') lines.append('- Delta != 0') lines.append('- three-line lock') lines.append('```') lines.append('') lines.append('## RESIDUAL') lines.append('') lines.append('```text') lines.append('R15/R16 = ' + str(residual['ratio'])) lines.append('```') lines.append('') lines.append('## FINAL DERIVATION') lines.append('') lines.append('```text') lines.append('3D structure') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('Projection relation') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('Three-line compression') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('B5-B6 selection') lines.append(' ↓') lines.append('META-EQUILIBRIUM') lines.append('```') write_text( SECTIONS['final'] / 'META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION_REPORT.md', '
'.join(lines) + '
' ) payload = { 'generated': iso_stamp(), 'pair_count': total_pairs, 'z_pass_pairs': z_pass_pairs, 'final_pass': True, 'symbolic': symbolic, 'residual': residual, 'meta': meta, } write_json( SECTIONS['final'] / 'META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION_REPORT.json', payload ) # ============================================================ # MAIN # ============================================================ def main(): if LOG_PATH.exists(): LOG_PATH.unlink() log_line('START META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION.py') pair_rows = build_pair_derivation() symbolic = build_symbolic_derivation() residual = build_residual_derivation() meta = build_meta_derivation(pair_rows) build_final_report( pair_rows, symbolic, residual, meta, ) log_line('SEQUENTIAL DERIVATION LOCK COMPLETE') log_line('OUTPUT=' + str(OUTPUT_ROOT)) log_line('END') if __name__ == '__main__': try: main() except Exception as exc: print('ERROR: ' + str(exc)) sys.exit(99) if os.name == 'nt': print('') input('Press Enter to close...') ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

all verifications into a common calibrated state.This state represents the point where: the structure is verified the residuals are verified the Z-system is verified the dataset is ready for the next step Collates all checks and generates the final reports used by subsequent verification layers.The code constitutes the second step in the complete verification chain.META_VESICA_CORE ↓ META_EQUILIBRIUM ↓ META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION ↓ FUSION_RESIDUAL_ANALYSIS ↓ STEP_ISOLATION ↓ COORDINATE_SYSTEM META_EQUILIBRIUM acts as the transition between data generation and formal verification.The code verifies that: the ABC system is intact all views are reproducible the Z-structure is stable the residual relation is unchanged tolerance checks pass the system reaches a stable core system is stable, reproducible and sufficiently verified to be used as the basis for all subsequent analyses. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See item.title: A. README
item.description: A. META VESICA CORE. PYTHON Link — 🔗. A. (M-V-C). PYTHON A. META_VESICA_CORE.py constitutes the first and most basic verification step in the RP9 chain.The code acts as the system's primary reference generator and is responsible for creating the complete dataset upon which all subsequent verification steps build.All subsequent analysis, residual review, sequence verification, step isolation, and coordinate reconstruction are derived from the data produced here.If this step is not correct, no subsequent verification can be considered valid.The code performs four main tasks:Creates the basic Vesica Piscis structure and generates the relational coordinates used throughout the rest of the system.Constructs the complete ABC system: A-series B-series C-series total of 20 basic views over 5 zoom levels.The result is 100 standardized observation points.Identifies and verifies the relational properties used in later steps: symmetry asymmetry projection center relation B5/B6 structure Z-passages Measures and documents the numerical residuals that arise during machine calculation.These residuals are later used as a reference for: Meta Equilibrium Fusion Analysis Step Isolation Coordinate System Verification The code is the starting point SECOND DIFFERENTIATION Harmonic Probe. PYTHON K6 constitutes the concluding module of the RP9 code-based verification framework.Where the previous verification modules establish, reproduce, validate and test the invariance of the relational structure, K6 demonstrates that additional observable phenomena can be positioned within the same verified relational architecture without modifying the underlying structure.Rather than introducing new relational principles, K6 extends the operational application of the existing framework.Its purpose is to demonstrate that previously verified relations remain sufficient to describe further operational observations.K6 performs the second operational differentiation of the RP9 framework.Beginning from the relational structure established throughout K1–K5, the module introduces an additional observational layer while preserving the complete relational organisation.The operational sequence can be summarized as:Established Structure ↓ Verified Invariance ↓ Second Differentiation ↓ Operational Positioning ↓ Relational Observation ↓ Verification The objective is not to generate a new structure, but to demonstrate that further observable quantities can be positioned within the same invariant relational framework.K6 represents the final operational layer of the RP9 verification sequence.Previous modules demonstrate that the relational structure can be: established, reproduced, verified, and shown to remain invariant. K6 extends this sequence by demonstrating that additional operational phenomena can be incorporated without altering the verified relational organisation.The emphasis therefore shifts from structural validation to relational positioning.K6 investigates whether additional operational quantities preserve the relational continuity established throughout the previous verification chain.Among the verified properties are: second relational differentiation, harmonic positioning, binary-triadic pulse continuity, seven-pass continuity, fine-structure positioning, machine residual consistency, operational reproducibility. Each verification examines whether the observed quantity occupies its expected position within the previously established relational framework.The operational chain follows the verified sequence:First Differentiation ↓ Half-Half Relation ↓ Binary-Triadic Pulse ↓ Seven Passage ↓ Fine Structure Constant ↓ Machine Residual ↓ Operational Verification Each layer depends upon the successful verification of the previous layer.No individual quantity is evaluated independently.Each observation is interpreted only within the established relational sequence.The complete verification chain becomes:K1 Primary Structure ↓ K2 Computational Reproduction ↓ K3 Relational Observation ↓ K4 Operational Verification ↓ K5 Structural Invariance Testing ↓ K6 Operational Positioning Each module extends the previous verification.No module replaces earlier results.K6 therefore represents the final operational extension of the verified framework.K6 does not: redefine the relational structure, introduce new structural principles, derive independent mathematical laws, replace previous verification modules. Instead, it demonstrates that previously established relational structures remain sufficient to position additional operational observations.The K6 package contains: operational source code, structured datasets, execution logs, reproducible presentations, verification reports, complete audit material. Every computational result may therefore be independently reproduced and verified.K6 concludes the RP9 code-based verification framework.Rather than introducing additional structural assumptions, the module demonstrates that further operational observations—including harmonic relations, binary-triadic behaviour, seven-pass continuity, the positioning of the fine-structure constant, and machine-level residuals—can all be incorporated into the same invariant relational architecture established by the preceding verification modules.Accordingly, K6 serves as the final operational confirmation that the RP9 framework remains internally consistent throughout the complete verification chain.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.

B. 333 & 666 Float Boundary Probe. FINAL REPORT Link — 🔗. B. 333 & 666 Float Boundary Probe. FINAL REPORT C. 333 & 666 Float Boundary Probe. PYTHON Link — 🔗.
C. 333 & 666 Float Boundary Probe. PYTHON This code constitutes the eighth and final verification in the RP9 sequence.All previous tests have verified relations, quotients, pulse structures and reconstruction properties through exact rational arithmetic.The purpose of the final test is to investigate what happens when the same structure is projected down into the machine's floating point storage.The focus is therefore shifted from:Relation to:Representation and from:Exact structure to:Machine representation The goal is to determine whether the observed:1/3 ↔ 2/3 -pulse can still be identified when expressed as IEEE-754 floating point.The code generates the sequence:q(n) = (3/4) / 2^n and:8 / q(n) for:40 iterations At each iteration, the:integer part and:remainder Then the:1/3 and:2/3 are verified against:float representation to measure the residual between:exact rational value and:machine-represented value In addition verified:2^-49 ↔ 2^-52 to check the previously identified quotient:8 in the machine store.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produce a stable pulse:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... However, these tests have mainly been performed with exact rational arithmetic.This test instead examines:What does the machine see? The question is no longer:Is the relation correct? but:How is the relation represented in the floating-point store? The test therefore functions as a bridge between:Exact mathematics and:Machine representation Basic relation:3/4 Operation model:q(n) = (3/4) / 2^n Check operation:8 / q(n) Number of iterations:40 Expected pulse:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... Verifications:1. Residue sequence 2. Float representation 3. Residue size 4. Residue order 5. Quotient between 2^-49 and 2^-52 If the model is correct, it is expected:All iterations PASS and:2/3 for even n 1/3 for odd n The residual is expected to be:non-zero because:1/3 and:2/3 cannot be represented exactly as IEEE-754 floating point numbers.In addition, it is expected that:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 to give an exact result.Number of iterations:40 Result:Residual sizes:1/3 ≈ −1.850371707708594 × 10^-17 2/3 ≈ −3.700743415417188 × 10^-17 Residual order:10^-17 Machine limit:2^-52 = 2.220446049250313e−16 2^-49 = 1.776356839400250e−15 Ratio:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 All checks:PASS The test passed.The observed:1/3 ↔ 2/3 -pulse survives all the way down to the machine layer.The machine does not represent:1/3 or:2/3 exactly.However, the residuals arise consistently and reproducibly.The result therefore shows that:The relation is preserved The representation is approximated and that:The residual is measurable, traceable and reproducible. In addition, it is verified again:1/8 ↔ 8 by:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 which gave an exact result.When run, the following is generated:rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe.py ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_run_trace.json ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_execution.log └── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_FINAL REPORT.md The JSON file contains:Full run trace All iterations Residual data Machine limits Verification status The log file contains:Start time End time Exit code The Markdown file contains:Complete final report This is the final verification in the recommended running order:1. rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test 2. rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check 3. rp9_start_independence_test 4. rp9_base_independence_test 5. rp9_perturbation_test 6. rp9_reverse_test 7. rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test 8. rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe The eight tests verify together:Origin ↓ Pulse ↓ Start-independent ↓ Base-independent ↓ Disruption resistance ↓ Reversibility ↓ Quota locking ↓ Machine representation The last test therefore serves as the final link between:Relational structure and:Actual machine representationentation of the same structure. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

C. Quotient Lock 1 Over 8 Test. PYTHON This code constitutes the seventh verification in the RP9 sequence.The previous tests have verified:R ↓ Rx8 ↓ 3/4 ↓ 1/3 ↔ 2/3 This verification instead focuses on the ratio that recurs throughout the chain:1/8 ↔ 8 The purpose is to determine whether this ratio remains exactly invariant through repeated scale steps and can thus serve as a stable lock value within the model.The code generates the sequence:R(0) = 1 R(n+1) = R(n) / 8 For each level, the following are verified:R(n+1) / R(n) and:R(n) / R(n+1) The requirement is that these should always give:1/8 respectively:8 without deviation.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produces a stable pulse.This test instead examines the underlying scaling relation.The question is:Is the ratio 1/8 ↔ 8 a consequence of single examples or is it invariant throughout the sequence? If the ratio remains exactly locked through all levels, the hypothesis that:1/8 ↔ 8 constitutes a fundamental scaling relationship in the tested model is strengthened.Starting value:R(0) = 1 Iteration:R(n+1) = R(n)/8 Verifications per level:R(n+1)/R(n) and:R(n)/R(n+1) Number of levels:101 Fit conditions:R(n+1)/R(n) = 1/8 and R(n)/R(n+1) = 8 for all levels.If the hypothesis is correct:1/8 returns at each downscaling.At the same time:8 return at each upscaling.Expected outcome matrix:Number of verified levels:101 Result:In addition, it was verified that:R16 / R15 = 1/8 R15 / R16 = 8 which also gave:PASS without deviation.The test was passed.The ratio:1/8 ↔ 8 remained exactly invariant through all verified levels.No iteration broke the relation.The result shows that:R(n+1)/R(n) and:R(n)/R(n+1) form an exactly reversible ratio structure within the investigated area.When executed, the following is generated:rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.py ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.json ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.log └── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test_FINALRAPPORT.md The JSON file contains all verified levels.The log file contains the execution history.The markdown file contains the summary verification report.The first seven tests have now verified:1. Origin reconstruction 2. Pulse invariance 3. Start independence 4. Base independence 5. Perturbation resistance 6. Reversibility 7. Quotient locking The next step will be:rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe Where the focus shifts from:relational structure to:machine representation The question changes from:Is the quotient invariant? to:How are 1/3 and 2/3 represented in actual IEEE-754 arithmetic? This will be the final verification of how the observed structure is projected into the machine's floating point memory. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.description:
B. Reverse Test. FINAL REPORT Link — 🔗. B. Reverse Test. FINAL REPORT C. Reverse Test. PYTHON Link — 🔗.
C. Reverse Test. PYTHON This code constitutes the sixth verification in the RP9 sequence.The previous tests have examined the forward structure:R ↓ Rx8 ↓ 3/4 ↓ 1/3 ↔ 2/3 This test reverses the direction.The purpose is to examine whether the observed residual pulse can be used to deduce possible original values.The test therefore serves as the first verification of the reversibility of the sequence.The code starts from the previously observed pulse sequence:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... Then a large number of possible candidate values ​​are tested:q = a/b to determine which ones reproduce exactly the same pulse.For each candidate, the following is performed:8 / (q / 2^n) during:8 iterations If the remainder follows:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... the candidate is accepted.If the sequence is broken, the candidate is rejected.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produces the observed residual pulse.This test examines the opposite question:If we only know the pulse, can we find the relationship? The test is therefore used to determine whether the pulse sequence contains sufficient information to reconstruct possible original values.Search range:1 ≤ numerator ≤ 64 1 ≤ denominator ≤ 64 Total number of candidates tested:4096 Fit condition:residual sequence = 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 over all:8 iterations Candidates that meet the condition are saved.Other candidates are discarded.If the pulse sequence is reproducible in reverse, it is expected that:at least one valid candidate is identified.If the sequence is also relationally stable, it is expected that:3/4 will be found among the approved candidates.Expected final status:PASS Number of candidates tested:4096 Number of candidates that reproduced the pulse:53 Among these were found:3/4 and several relationally closely related candidates.Example:3/64 3/31 3/16 3/10 3/7 3/4 3 12 All of these reproduced the observed pulse sequence within the limits of the test.Final status:PASS The test passed.The observed pulse sequence can be used to identify candidate values ​​that reproduce the same behavior.The result shows that:pulse ↓ candidatevalue is possible as an operation.This verifies that the sequence not only works forwards but can also be analyzed backwards.The test does not prove that:3/4 is the only possible candidate.However, the test shows that:3/4 is included in the set of values ​​that exactly reproduce the observed pulse within the tested range.When run, the following is generated:rp9_reverse_test │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_reverse_test.py ├── rp9_reverse_test.json ├── rp9_reverse_test.log └── rp9_reverse_test_FINALREPORT.md The JSON file contains all identified candidates.The log file contains the run history.The Markdown file contains the summary verification report.The first six tests have now verified:1. Origin reconstruction 2. Pulse invariance 3. Start independence 4. Base independence 5. Perturbation resistance 6. Reversibility The next step will be:rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test Where the focus shifts from:relations to:quotients The question changes from:Can the sequence be run backwards? to:Is the quotient 1/8 ↔ 8 invariant throughout the system? This will be the first direct verification of the quotient locking that recurs throughout the RP9 sequence. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.description:
B. RP9. Binary pulse invariance check. FINAL REPORT Link — 🔗. B. RP9. Binary pulse invariance check. FINAL REPORT C. Binary Pulse Invariance Check. PYTHON Link — 🔗.
C. Binary Pulse Invariance Check. PYTHON This code is the second verification in the RP9 chain.After the previous test has shown that different representative R values ​​can be normalized to the same structure, this code examines whether the resulting pulse is stable over time.The purpose is to determine whether the alternation:1/3 ↔ 2/3 is a temporary numerical effect or a reproducible invariant structure.The code starts from the relation:3/4 and generates the sequence:q_n = (3/4) / 2^n For each iteration, the following is calculated:8 / q_n Then the following is extracted: the integer part the remainder The remainder is then compared against:1/3 2/3 and the expected change:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... over 100 iterations.If the observed pulse is truly a structural feature, it must survive repeated iterations.The test therefore examines:3/4 ↓ (3/4)/2^n ↓ 8/q_n ↓ remainder to determine whether:1/3 ↔ 2/3 is invariant.If the pulse breaks at any iteration, there is no support for treating it as a stable structure.If the pulse never breaks, the hypothesis that it is a recurring feature of the operation under investigation is strengthened.Input value:3/4 Operation:q_n = (3/4) / 2^n Check:8 / q_n Iterations:100 Fit conditions:remainder ∈ {1/3, 2/3} and:even n -> 2/3 odd n -> 1/3 Exact rational arithmetic is used through:fractions.Fraction which eliminates rounding errors during the verification itself.If the hypothesis is correct, it is expected that: all iterations pass the remainder be 1/3 or 2/3 the alternation follow the same pattern throughout the test no iteration breaks the sequence Expected final status:PASS The result was:During all iterations it was observed:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... without interruption.The test was passed.For the investigated operation:3/4 ↓ (3/4)/2^n ↓ 8/q_n produces a residual pulse that remains invariant through all verified iterations.The result shows that the pulse does not occur as a single numerical outcome but as a reproducible property of the tested sequence.When run, the following is generated:rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check.py ├── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check_SLUTRAPPORT.md └── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check_run_trace.json The JSON file contains the complete run history.The Markdown report contains the verification result.The Python file contains the reproducible test implementation.This verification shows that the pulse exists and remains stable through iteration.The next question becomes:Does it matter how 3/4 is represented? Therefore continue to:rp9_start_independence_test There it is verified whether the same pulse arises from:3/4 6/8 12/16 24/32 48/64 ... and thus whether the structure is independent of starting resolution and representation. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.
